130	### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
131	- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
132	- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
133	- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
134	- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
135	- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
136	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).
137	
138	### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
139	Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
140	1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
141	2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
142	- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
143	- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
144	- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
145	- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
146	- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
147	- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
148	- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
149	- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
150	- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
151	- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.

167	- Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
168	- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
169	- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. # Phase 3 Review: "Semantics and execution" (T7 analyzer/plan, T8 executor/API)

**Phase verdict: READY TO ADVANCE.** I found no blocking issues in either task. Both tasks PASS.

I had no shell in this review, so I did not run the tests myself. The test results below are your recorded results for the current tree. My own evidence comes from tracing the code line by line against `contract.md`, spec §5.5–§5.9 and §5.12, and plan §3.7, §3.8 and §3.10.

---

## T7: Semantic analyzer and bound plan — PASS

**Defined tests:** `compileall` exited 0. `pytest -q tests/test_analyzer.py tests/test_parser.py tests/test_catalog.py` gave 220 passed, 1 skipped. The skip is the case-variant-file test in `test_catalog`, which was already there before this phase.

| AC | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC7, type mismatch at the operator | Met | `analyzer.py:269-271`: `name + 1` gives `'+' to TEXT and INTEGER` at the `+` token, column 13. Tested by `test_ac7_type_mismatch`. |
| AC6/AC10, output names | Met | `analyzer.py:108-117`. The alias is used as written. An unparenthesized `ColumnRef` gives `headers[b.index]`, so `select NAME … E.Id` gives `name`. Anything else gives `sql[item.start:item.end]`, and the parser span (`sqlparser.py:130`) excludes the alias. So `(id)`, `COUNT(*)` and `salary * 2` come out verbatim. |
| Every Semantic template at its exact position | Met | 53 cases in `ERRORS` (`tests/test_analyzer.py:86-151`). Positions checked against the code: second range-name token via `ref.range_pos` (`:94`); column-ref start (`:224-226`); function name (`:282,287,293`); the `*` in a call (`:285`); condition start (`:212`); the `*` or `t.*` star (`:188`); the ordinal (`:141`); the ESCAPE string (`:267`); the `IN`/`LIKE` token (D9). |
| ON scope | Met | `scope[:i + 2]` at `:102`. Tested by the `d2.code` and `e2.name` rows. |
| Structural identity | Met | `_key` (`:48-66`). Columns compare by flat index, so qualified and unqualified references are equal. Parens are dropped at bind time (`:232`). Literals compare by (type, value), so `1` ≠ `1.0`. `<>` is treated as `!=` (D8). Aggregates compare by upper-case name plus argument key. `group_level` (`:161-183`) checks the group key first, then aggregate, then literal; any other bare column is an error. |
| Static result types | Met | Arithmetic type rule at `:274`. Unary keeps its operand type (`:247`). Predicates are always INTEGER. SUM keeps the argument type, AVG is REAL, MIN/MAX keep the argument type, COUNT is INTEGER, and the D3/D4 NULL cases hold (`:289-296`). LEFT JOIN columns keep their static type (D2). |
| IO errors in FROM order | Met | Load, then duplicate check, in the order of `refs` (`:88-99`). Only referenced tables are loaded. |
| ORDER BY alias, ordinal, expression | Met | `:137-151`. A bare INTEGER `Literal` is an ordinal; `(1)` and `-1` fall through as expressions. A bare unqualified `ColumnRef` matching exactly one alias is an alias reference; two matches give `ambiguous column`. The DISTINCT rule is at `:195-200` and is checked against the select keys taken before the group-level rewrite. |

I also checked these and they are correct:
- Aggregate-query detection includes aggregates nested anywhere in the select list or ORDER BY (`:154-155`).
- Nested aggregates and aggregates in WHERE/ON/GROUP BY are rejected at the inner function name (`:286-288`).
- Unknown function is reported before the `*` rule (D16).
- The ESCAPE length check counts code points.

## T8: Executor and library API — PASS

**Defined tests:** `compileall` exited 0. `pytest -q tests/test_executor.py tests/test_api.py tests/test_analyzer.py tests/test_evaluate.py tests/test_imports.py` gave 225 passed. The full suite gave 421 passed, 1 skipped.

| AC | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC11, AC2, AC3, `tables()` | Met | AVG is `total / count` with true division (`executor.py:122-123`): 380/4 = 95.0, type REAL. `schema` returns `list(zip(columns, types))` (`api.py:45`). `tables()` sorts by `(lower(), name)` (`catalog.py:47`). |
| AC5, AC6, AC8, AC9, AC10 rows | Met | `test_acceptance_rows`. AC8 uses truncating integer division and dividend-sign `%` (`evaluate.py:35-39`). `NULL / 0` is checked for NULL first. |
| Join order, LEFT JOIN fill, NULL never matches | Met | `executor.py:132-147`. ON is evaluated for every pair; one NULL-filled row follows the pairs of an unmatched left row. Tests: `INNER`/LEFT expectations (`tests/test_executor.py:64-91`) and `test_on_evaluated_for_every_pair`. |
| Duplicate names, re-read on each execute, PathLike | Met | `test_duplicate_output_names`, `test_files_reread_each_execute`, `test_connect_pathlike`. The catalog uses `os.fspath`. |
| GROUP BY, HAVING, empty input | Met | Without GROUP BY, one group is pre-seeded with key `()`; with GROUP BY, groups are a first-seen dict (`:160`). """Stdlib-only guard: every import in minisql/*.py must be in the allowlist; never sqlite3."""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import glob
import os

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

# Explicit stdlib allowlist (do not use sys.stdlib_module_names; Python 3.9 lacks it).
# Tasks listing this file in scope may extend it with stdlib modules only.
STDLIB_ALLOWLIST = frozenset(
    """
    __future__ argparse codecs collections contextlib csv dataclasses decimal enum errno
    functools glob io itertools locale math numbers operator os pathlib re shutil signal
    stat string sys textwrap traceback types typing unicodedata warnings weakref
    """.split()
)


def _module_files():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "minisql", "*.py")))
    assert files, "no minisql/*.py files found"
    return files


def _imported_top_levels(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        tree = ast.parse(f.read(), filename=path)
    names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                names.add(alias.name.split(".")[0])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.level:  # relative import: within the package
                continue
            names.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
    return names


def test_only_stdlib_imports():
    bad = {}
    for path in _module_files():
        extra = _imported_top_levels(path) - STDLIB_ALLOWLIST - {"minisql"}
        if extra:
            bad[os.path.basename(path)] = sorted(extra)
    assert bad == {}


def test_no_sqlite3():
    assert "sqlite3" not in STDLIB_ALLOWLIST
    for path in _module_files():
        assert "sqlite3" not in _imported_top_levels(path), path


def test_guard_detects_forbidden_import(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "x.py"
    p.write_text("import sqlite3\nfrom os import path\nfrom . import y\nimport numpy.linalg\n")
    assert _imported_top_levels(str(p)) == {"sqlite3", "os", "numpy"}

- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. A column of type NULL holds only NULL cells (left-aligned).

### 5.11 CLI and REPL (R19, R20)
- `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`; argparse with `allow_abbrev=False`, `--data` default `.`, `--format` `choices=['csv','table']` default `None` (one-shot → csv, REPL → table), positional `sql` `nargs='?'`; `args.sql is not None` → one-shot (so `""` is one-shot with empty SQL). - One-shot: `connect` first (missing DIR → `IOError: …` exit 3 before lexing); execute; format the full output string, then write once. Errors: stdout empty, stderr exactly `str(err) + "\n"`; exit 1 for Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime, 3 for IO, 0 on success.
- Top-level guard: catch `MiniSQLError`; catch `BrokenPipeError` (redirect stdout to devnull, exit 1); `KeyboardInterrupt` (exit 130); any other unexpected `Exception` (e.g. `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`) → a single line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <exception text>` on stderr, exit 1 (D19) — never a traceback.
- REPL: prompt `minisql> ` when buffer empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces) otherwise, written to stdout without newline and flushed, regardless of TTY. Input not echoed. Read lines with `readline()`; strip one trailing `\n` only (keep `\r`; D18). With an empty buffer: a line whose stripped text (strip `' \t\r\n'`) starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise append the line (joined with `\n`); when the buffer right-stripped ends with `;`, execute it and clear the buffer.

Anything else (incl. `.format` with a bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).

### CLI

`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.

### REPL

- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.

### Exit codes (one-shot)

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
| 3 | IOError |

On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.

## Error handling

Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.

Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.

| Kind | Message templates | Position |
|---|---|---|
| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |

# T9 notes — one-shot CLI, stream setup, exit codes, no-traceback guard

Status: DONE (uncommitted). Base HEAD 2a6e585. Python 3.9.6. 2026-11-04T09:58Z.

## Design
- `minisql/cli.py`
  - `_setup_streams()` is called at the start of `main()` and never at import. It reconfigures stdout/stderr (`utf-8`, `backslashreplace`, `newline='\n'`) and stdin (`utf-8`, `replace`, `newline='\n'`), each guarded by `hasattr(reconfigure)` plus try/except (D18).
  - `_parser()`: `ArgumentParser(prog='minisql', allow_abbrev=False)`, `--data` (default `.`), `--format` (choices csv/table, default None), positional `sql` (`nargs='?'`). Usage errors raise `SystemExit(2)` from `parse_args`, which is not caught.
  - `_run(args)`: `connect(args.data)` runs first, so IO fails with exit 3 before lexing, in both one-shot and REPL mode (D21). With no SQL it lazily imports `minisql.repl.run_repl(conn, args.format or 'table', sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr)`. Otherwise it runs execute, then format_table if `--format table`, else format_csv. The text is written once and flushed, giving 0. On `MiniSQLError`, stderr gets `str(err)+'\n'` and the exit is 3 for IO, else 1. stdout stays empty because output is only written after formatting succeeds.
  - Guard in `main()`: `BrokenPipeError` → dup2 devnull onto stdout's fd, return 1. `KeyboardInterrupt` → 130 (silent). Any other `Exception` → `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <str(exc) or type name>`, return 1 (D19).
- `minisql/__main__.py`: already `sys.exit(main())` from T1, so it is unchanged and final.
- `minisql/repl.py`: new minimal stub `run_repl(conn, fmt, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int` returning 0. T10 replaces it.
- `tests/test_scaffold.py`: the placeholder assertion (`run_cli([]) == (0, b'', b'')` at the repo root) is replaced by `test_cli_runs_as_module`. That test runs REPL mode with empty stdin (rc 0, empty stderr; stdout is not asserted, so T10 prompts remain compatible) plus a one-shot `SELECT 1 AS one`.
- `tests/test_imports.py`: unchanged (argparse and os are already allowlisted).

## Known argparse limitation (documented, not worked around)
An SQL argument that starts with `--` and contains no space (e.g. `--x`) is parsed as an option, giving exit 2. Users can pass `--` before the SQL argument (`python -m minisql -- "--x"`). `-- comment\nSELECT 1` works because argparse treats arguments that start with `-` and contain a space as positionals. Tested in `test_sql_starting_with_dash_comment` and `test_double_dash_separator`.

## Technical Notes:
- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces, then `...> `) otherwise; written to stdout without newline and flushed before each read, regardless of TTY. Input is not echoed.
- Read with `stdin.readline()`; `''` = EOF. Remove exactly one trailing `\n` (keep `\r`, D18).
- Empty buffer: if `line.strip(' \t\r\n')` starts with `.` → command; if it is empty → ignored. Otherwise append the line to the buffer (joined with `\n`); when `buffer.rstrip(' \t\r\n')` ends with `;` → execute the buffer text and clear it. Non-empty buffer: every line (incl. blank or starting with `.`) is appended.
- Commands (compare the stripped line; command word exact lower-case): `.help` → free help text to stdout (ends with `\n`); `.tables` → `conn.tables()` one per line; `.schema NAME` → `name TYPE` per line from `conn.schema(NAME)` (errors → one stderr line); `.format csv` / `.format table` → switch format; `.quit` / `.exit` → return 0. Anything else (unknown, `.format` with bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>\n` (D20). Split arguments on whitespace (`' \t'`).
- Execution: `result = conn.execute(buffer)`; print `format_csv` (no footer) or `format_table` per current format to stdout. On `MiniSQLError`: flush stdout, write `str(err) + '\n'` to stderr, continue (positions relative to the buffer). Unexpected exceptions → one-line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` and continue (D19).
- EOF: if the buffer is non-empty, execute it (same output/error handling); then return 0 with nothing further printed (no extra prompt or newline).
- Example transcript (stdin `SELECT 1 AS one;\n`, table format): stdout `minisql> one\n---\n  1\n(1 row)\nminisql> ` — verify exact expected strings against T6 formatting in tests.
- Contract: REPL. Exit code 0 at EOF/.quit.

## Acceptance Criteria:

* stdin `SELECT 1 AS one;\n` with default (table) format → stdout = `minisql> ` + table text + `minisql> `; exit 0; stderr empty.
* Multi-line statement: `SELECT\n1;\n` → prompts `minisql> ` then `   ...> ` then result then `minisql> `.
* `.format csv` then a query → CSV without footer; `.tables` lists `dept`, `emp`; `.schema emp` prints `id INTEGER`, `name TEXT`, `dept TEXT`, `salary INTEGER`.
* Unknown command `.foo bar` → stderr `unknown command: .foo bar\n`, session continues.
* Error query `SELECT 1 # 2;` → stderr one line `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`, session continues; multi-line buffer error positions are relative to the buffer (line 2 etc.).

"""Command-line entry point: one-shot query or REPL; exit codes 0/1/2/3, never a traceback."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

from .api import connect
from .errors import MiniSQLError
from .formatting import format_csv, format_table


def _setup_streams() -> None:
    """D18: UTF-8 with '\\n' on every platform, whatever PYTHONIOENCODING says."""
    for stream, errors in ((sys.stdout, "backslashreplace"), (sys.stderr, "backslashreplace"),
                           (sys.stdin, "replace")):
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
            try:
                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=errors, newline="\n")
            except Exception:  # replaced/closed streams (e.g. under test harnesses)
                pass


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="minisql", allow_abbrev=False)
    p.add_argument("--data", default=".", metavar="DIR", help="directory of CSV tables (default: .)")
    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["csv", "table"], default=None,
                   help="output format (one-shot default: csv; REPL default: table)")
    p.add_argument("sql", nargs="?", default=None, metavar="SQL", help="query to run; omit for the REPL")
    return p


def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        conn = connect(args.data)
        if args.sql is None:
            from .repl import run_repl
            return run_repl(conn, args.format or "table", sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr)
        result = conn.execute(args.sql)
        text = format_table(result) if args.format == "table" else format_csv(result)
    except MiniSQLError as err:
        sys.stderr.write(str(err) + "\n")
        sys.stderr.flush()
        return 3 if err.kind == "IO" else 1
    sys.stdout.write(text)
    sys.stdout.flush()
    return 0


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    _setup_streams()
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)  # usage errors: SystemExit(2) propagates
    try:
        return _run(args)
    except BrokenPipeError:
        try:
            os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())
        except Exception:
            pass
        return 1
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 130
    except Exception as exc:  # D19: one RuntimeError line, never a traceback
        try:
            sys.stderr.write("RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s\n" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))
            sys.stderr.flush()
        except Exception:
            pass
        return 1

"""Library API: connect(data_dir) -> Connection with execute / tables / schema."""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from typing import List, Tuple

from .analyzer import analyze
from .catalog import Catalog
from .errors import MiniSQLError, QueryRuntimeError, SemanticError
from .executor import execute
from .result import Result
from .sqlparser import parse

_RECURSION_LIMIT = 10000


def connect(data_dir) -> "Connection":
    """`data_dir` is a str or os.PathLike; a missing or non-directory path raises DataIOError now."""
    return Connection(data_dir)


class Connection:
    def __init__(self, data_dir):
        self._catalog = Catalog(data_dir)

    def execute(self, sql: str) -> Result:
        old = sys.getrecursionlimit()
        sys.setrecursionlimit(max(old, _RECURSION_LIMIT))
        try:
            return execute(analyze(parse(sql), sql, self._catalog), sql)
        except MiniSQLError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:  # D19: RecursionError, OverflowError, int/str limits, ...
            raise QueryRuntimeError(str(exc) or type(exc).__name__, 1, 1) from None
        finally:
            sys.setrecursionlimit(old)

    def tables(self) -> List[str]:
        return self._catalog.table_names()

    def schema(self, table: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        t = self._catalog.load(table)
        if t is None:
            raise SemanticError("unknown table '%s'" % table, 1, 1)
        return list(zip(t.columns, t.types))

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import glob
import os

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

# Explicit stdlib allowlist (do not use sys.stdlib_module_names; Python 3.9 lacks it).
# Tasks listing this file in scope may extend it with stdlib modules only.
STDLIB_ALLOWLIST = frozenset(
    """
    __future__ argparse codecs collections contextlib csv dataclasses decimal enum errno
    functools glob io itertools locale math numbers operator os pathlib re shutil signal
    stat string sys textwrap traceback types typing unicodedata warnings weakref
    """.split()
)


def _module_files():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "minisql", "*.py")))
    assert files, "no minisql/*.py files found"
    return files


def _imported_top_levels(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        tree = ast.parse(f.read(), filename=path)
    names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                names.add(alias.name.split(".")[0])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.level:  # relative import: within the package
                continue
            names.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
    return names


def test_only_stdlib_imports():

        extra = _imported_top_levels(path) - STDLIB_ALLOWLIST - {"minisql"}
        if extra:

    assert bad == {}

def format_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    lines = [",".join(_csv_field(name) for name in result.columns)]
    for row in result.rows:
        lines.append(
            ",".join(_csv_field(value_text(v, t)) for v, t in zip(row, result.types))
        )
    return "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)


def _escape(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r")


def format_table(result: Result) -> str:
    headers = [_escape(name) for name in result.columns]
    body = []
    for row in result.rows:
        cells = []
        for v, t in zip(row, result.types):
            text = value_text(v, t)
            cells.append((_escape(text), t in _NUMERIC) if text is not None else ("NULL", False))
        body.append(cells)
    widths = [len(h) for h in headers]
    for cells in body:
        for i, (text, _) in enumerate(cells):
            widths[i] = max(widths[i], len(text))
    lines = [
        " | ".join(h.ljust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, widths)),
        "-+-".join("-" * w for w in widths),
    ]
    for cells in body:
        lines.append(
            " | ".join(
                text.rjust(w) if right else text.ljust(w)
                for (text, right), w in zip(cells, widths)
            )

"""T10: interactive REPL (subprocess bytes-mode transcripts plus direct run_repl calls)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import io

from minisql import connect
from minisql.formatting import format_csv, format_table
from minisql.repl import run_repl

P = b"minisql> "
C = b"   ...> "


def _table(data_dir, sql):
    return format_table(connect(str(data_dir)).execute(sql)).encode("utf-8")


def _csv(data_dir, sql):
    return format_csv(connect(str(data_dir)).execute(sql)).encode("utf-8")


def _repl(run_cli, data_dir, stdin, *extra):
    return run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), *extra], stdin=stdin)


def test_single_statement_table_default(run_cli, data_dir):
    table = _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one")
    assert table == b"one\n---\n  1\n(1 row)\n"
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 AS one;\n") == (0, P + table + P, b"")


def test_multi_line_statement(run_cli, data_dir):
    table = _table(data_dir, "SELECT\n1;")
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT\n1;\n") == (0, P + C + table + P, b"")


def test_commands_format_tables_schema(run_cli, data_dir):
    stdin = b".format csv\nSELECT name FROM emp WHERE id < 3;\n.tables\n.schema emp\n.help\n"
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, stdin)
    assert (rc, err) == (0, b"")
    csv = _csv(data_dir, "SELECT name FROM emp WHERE id < 3")
    assert csv == b"name\nAnn\nBob\n"
    expected_prefix = (
        P + P + csv + P + b"dept\nemp\n" + P
        + b"id INTEGER\nname TEXT\ndept TEXT\nsalary INTEGER\n" + P
    )
    assert out.startswith(expected_prefix) and out.endswith(b"\n" + P)
    assert len(out) > len(expected_prefix) + len(P)  # .help printed something


def test_format_table_switch_back(run_cli, data_dir):
    stdin = b".format csv\n.format table\nSELECT 1 AS one;\n"
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, stdin) == (0, P * 3 + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one") + P, b"")


def test_cli_format_csv_starts_repl_in_csv(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 AS one;\n", "--format", "csv")
    assert (rc, out, err) == (0, P + b"one\n1\n" + P, b"")


def test_unknown_and_malformed_commands(run_cli, data_dir):
    stdin = b".foo bar\n  .format xml \n.format\n.schema\n.TABLES\nSELECT 1 AS one;\n"
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, stdin)
    assert rc == 0
    assert err == (
        b"unknown command: .foo bar\n"
        b"unknown command: .format xml\n"
        b"unknown command: .format\n"
        b"unknown command: .schema\n"
        b"unknown command: .TABLES\n"
    )
    assert out == P * 6 + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one") + P


def test_schema_unknown_table_error_line(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b".schema nope\n")
    assert (rc, out) == (0, P + P)
    assert err.count(b"\n") == 1 and err.startswith(b"SemanticError at line 1, column 1: ")


def test_error_query_continues(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 # 2;\nSELECT 1 AS one;\n")
    assert rc == 0
    assert err == b"LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'\n"
    assert out == P + P + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one") + P


def test_error_positions_relative_to_buffer(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1;\nSELECT\n1 # 2;\n")
    assert rc == 0
    assert err == b"LexError at line 2, column 3: unexpected character '#'\n"
    assert out == P + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1") + P + C + P


def test_blank_lines_ignored_and_buffer_keeps_dot_lines(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"\n  \t\nSELECT 1 AS one\n\n.5 AS x;\n")
    assert (rc, err) == (0, b"")
    assert out == P * 3 + C + C + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one\n\n.5 AS x;") + P


def test_quit_and_exit_stop_immediately(run_cli, data_dir):
    for cmd in (b".quit", b".exit", b"  .quit  "):
        assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, cmd + b"\nSELECT 1;\n") == (0, P, b"")


def test_eof_executes_pending_buffer(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1") == (0, P + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1"), b"")
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT\n1")
    assert (rc, out, err) == (0, P + C + _table(data_dir, "SELECT\n1"), b"")


def test_eof_pending_buffer_error(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 #")
    assert (rc, out) == (0, P)
    assert err == b"LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'\n"


def test_empty_stdin(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"") == (0, P, b"")


def test_missing_data_dir_no_prompt(run_cli, tmp_path):
    rc, out, err = run_cli(["--data", "missing"], stdin=b"SELECT 1;\n", cwd=tmp_path)
    assert (rc, out, err) == (3, b"", b"IOError: data directory not found: missing\n")


def test_crlf_input_byte_identical(run_cli, data_dir):
    lf = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1;\n.tables\nSELECT\n1;\n.quit\n")
    crlf = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1;\r\n.tables\r\nSELECT\r\n1;\r\n.quit\r\n")
    assert lf == crlf
    assert lf[0] == 0 and lf[2] == b""


def test_direct_run_repl_stringio(data_dir):
    stdin = io.StringIO("SELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1;\n.format csv\nSELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1;\n")
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    assert run_repl(connect(str(data_dir)), "table", stdin, out, err) == 0
    conn = connect(str(data_dir))
    r = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1")
    assert out.getvalue() == "minisql> " + format_table(r) + "minisql> minisql> " + format_csv(r) + "minisql> "
    assert err.getvalue() == ""


def test_direct_unexpected_exception_one_line(data_dir):
    class Boom:
        def execute(self, sql):
            raise ValueError("boom")

        def tables(self):
            raise KeyError("k")

    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    assert run_repl(Boom(), "table", io.StringIO("SELECT 1;\n.tables\n"), out, err) == 0
    assert err.getvalue() == (
        "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: boom\n"
        "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: 'k'\n"
    )
    assert out.getvalue() == "minisql> " * 3

# T10 — Interactive REPL: implementation notes (geeky-coder)

Verdict: DONE. Tested state: HEAD 2a6e585 plus uncommitted T9 work (input) and T10 files below. Python 3.9.6, darwin.

## Design (minisql/repl.py)
- `run_repl(conn, fmt, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int` replaces the T9 stub. Signature and the cli.py call site are unchanged, so **cli.py was not edited**.
- Loop: write the prompt (`minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, otherwise `   ...> `) and flush; `stdin.readline()`; `''` = EOF. Remove one trailing `\n` only, so `\r` stays (D18).
- Empty buffer: `line.strip(' \t\r\n')`. If that is empty the line is ignored. If it starts with `.` it is a command. Otherwise the line starts the buffer. Non-empty buffer: every line is appended with `\n`. Execute when `buffer.rstrip(' \t\r\n').endswith(';')`.
- Commands: the stripped line is split on `[ \t]+` (re). Exact lower-case words with exact arity. `.quit`/`.exit` (no args) return 0. `.help` prints a fixed text ending in `\n`. `.tables` prints one name per line. `.schema NAME` prints `name TYPE` per line. `.format csv|table` switches the format. Everything else (wrong arity, bad argument, unknown word, upper case) writes `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).
- Errors (`_guarded`): `MiniSQLError` gives `str(err)`. Any other `Exception` gives `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text or type name>` (D19). stdout is flushed before each stderr write, and the session continues. Positions are relative to the buffer because the buffer text is passed to `conn.execute`.
- EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed with the same handling, then the function returns 0 and prints nothing more. Note: a prompt precedes every read, so the read that hits EOF on a pending buffer comes after a `   ...> ` prompt (for example stdin `SELECT 1` gives `minisql>    ...> ` + table). This follows the contract rule "prompt ... flushed before each read".
- BrokenPipeError and KeyboardInterrupt propagate to the existing cli.main handlers (exit 1 / 130).
- Imports: `re` plus package-relative imports only; `re` is already on the allowlist, so test_imports.py is unchanged. test_scaffold.py is unchanged because no assertion conflicts (it checks only rc and stderr for empty stdin).

## Tests (tests/test_repl.py, 18 tests)
Subprocess bytes-mode transcripts. Expected result text comes from `format_table`/`format_csv` (T6), and the table literal `one\n---\n  1\n(1 row)\n` is pinned. Coverage: single statement; multi-line; `.format csv` + query, `.tables`, `.schema emp`, `.help`; switching back to table; `--format csv` REPL; unknown/malformed commands (`.foo bar`, `.format xml`, `.format`, `.schema`, `.TABLES`); `.schema nope` gives one SemanticError line; LexError `SELECT 1 # 2;` and the session continues; buffer-relative line 2 position; blank lines ignored and a `.`-line kept inside the buffer; `.quit`/`.exit` exit immediately; EOF executes a pending buffer (OK and error cases); empty stdin; `--data missing` gives exit 3 with no prompt; CRLF vs LF byte-identical; direct `run_repl` with StringIO; an unexpected exception gives a single RuntimeError line.

- AC2 multi-line: test_multi_line_statement

content.content:
# minisql: Contract

## Constraints

- Stack: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
- Package location: `minisql/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`), with `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`.
- Entry points: `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` from repo root; `import minisql; minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
- Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser.

## Functional requirements

- **R1** Importable as `minisql`, runnable as `python -m minisql`; standard-library imports only, never `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser.
- **R2** Tables load from the data directory per the data contract.
- **R3** Column types are inferred per the inference rules; empty fields are NULL.
- **R4** The tokenizer implements the lexical rules.
- **R5** The parser implements the grammar and precedence table.
- **R6** Keywords and all names resolve case-insensitively.
- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.
- **R11** INNER and LEFT joins follow nested-loop semantics and order.
- **R12** Grouping, `HAVING` and aggregates follow the aggregate rules, including empty input.
- **R13** `DISTINCT` keeps first occurrences.
- **R14** `ORDER BY` supports aliases, ordinals, expressions, multiple keys, `ASC`/`DESC`; NULLs smallest; stable ties.
- **R15** `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take non-negative integer literals.
- **R16** Clauses evaluate in the defined order; `AND`/`OR` short-circuit.
- **R17** The library API matches the contract.
- **R18** CSV and table formats match byte-for-byte.
- **R19** The one-shot CLI follows the output and exit-code rules.
- **R20** The REPL follows the prompt, buffering, command and exit rules.
- **R21** Errors use the specified classes, format, templates and positions.

## Language reference

### Lexical rules

- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.

### Grammar (EBNF)

```
query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
and       = not {"AND" not} ;
not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
colref    = name ["." name] ;
name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
```

`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.

### Precedence (highest first)

| Level | Operators | Associativity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
| 5 | `NOT` | right |
| 6 | `AND` | left |
| 7 | `OR` | left |

### Types and values

- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.

### NULL and predicates

- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.

### Type inference

For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.

## Interface contract

### Data directory

- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.

### Name resolution and output names

- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

### Aggregates and grouping

- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.

### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT

- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.

### Evaluation order

1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.

`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.

### Library API

```python
minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
```

`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.

### Output formats

Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.

**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.

**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.

### CLI

`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.

### REPL

- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.

### Exit codes (one-shot)

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
| 3 | IOError |

On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.

## Error handling

Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.

Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.

| Kind | Message templates | Position |
|---|---|---|
| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |

`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.

## Acceptance criteria

Fixture `emp.csv`: `id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`. Fixture `dept.csv`: `code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`.

- **AC1** (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
- **AC2** (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
- **AC3** (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
- **AC4** (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
- **AC5** (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
- **AC6** (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann` (header from the CSV, not the query).
- **AC7** (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
- **AC8** (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
- **AC9** (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
- **AC10** (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
- **AC11** (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
- **AC12** (R2-R21) Behaviour specified in the Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections is reproduced exactly (byte-for-byte output, exit codes and error lines) by hidden tests.

275:## Research basis and citations
Each subsection restates the governing contract rule and adds the binding design decisions. Decision IDs (Dn) are collected in §5.12.

### 5.1 Errors and positions (R21)
- `MiniSQLError(Exception)` with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`. `str(err)` = `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO: `IOError: <message>`. Kind `Runtime` prints `RuntimeError at …` (class name `QueryRuntimeError`).
- All positions derive from an absolute code-point offset into the SQL text via one helper: `line = sql.count('\n', 0, off) + 1`; `column = off - (sql.rfind('\n', 0, off) + 1) + 1`. Lines split on `\n` only; tab and `\r` count as one column (Domain Expert F1).
- Message templates and positions exactly per the contract table (Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO). `N`, `R`, `F` as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`); `OP` as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates.
- Phase order: lex the whole input → parse fully → semantic (including IO for referenced tables in FROM order) → execute. All static errors are raised before any row is evaluated.

### 5.2 Lexer (R4, R6)
- Whitespace exactly space, tab, `\r`, `\n`; anything else outside a token (e.g. NBSP, form feed, `#`, lone `!`) → `unexpected character 'X'` at that character.
- `--` comment to end of line (so `SELECT --1` is followed by EOF).
- Character classes are ASCII-only: identifiers `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; digits `[0-9]`. Never `str.isdigit/isalpha/isidentifier` or `\d` (Integration F25–26, Domain Expert F1).
- Keywords (case-insensitive, reserved): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`. Function names are identifiers.
- Quoted identifier `"..."` (`""` → `"`), may contain anything incl. newlines, may equal a keyword; unterminated → `unterminated quoted identifier` at the opening quote.
- String `'...'` (`''` → `'`), may span lines, backslash literal; unterminated → `unterminated string literal` at opening quote.
- Numbers: INTEGER `[0-9]+`; REAL `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. Longest match of these forms; if the next character is an ASCII letter, digit, `_` or `.` → `invalid number literal` at the literal start. Thus `12abc`, `1e`, `1e+`, `1..2`, `1.2.3`, `1_0`, `1.5e` are errors; `1.`, `1.e5`, `.5` are valid; `.` not followed by a digit is the `.` operator. REAL value = `float(text)`, INTEGER value = `int(text)`.
- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . ;` and `*`.
- Each token carries `kind`, `value`, `text = sql[start:end]`, `start`, `end`. An EOF token sits at offset `len(sql)` ("one past last input character").

### 5.3 Parser (R5)
- Recursive descent over the contract EBNF. Level 4 (comparison / IS / LIKE / IN) is non-associative: `cmp` parses at most one tail; a second comparison operator surfaces as `unexpected token '<text>'` at that operator (`a = b = c`, `a IS NULL IS NULL`).
- `NOT` binds looser than comparison (`NOT 1 = 2` = `NOT (1 = 2)` → 1); `1 = NOT 2` → ParseError at `NOT`.
- `unexpected token 'T'` uses the token's exact source text (strings keep their quotes, keywords keep written case). At EOF: `unexpected end of input` at offset `len(sql)`.
- Calls: `name "(" ("*" | expr) ")"`; whitespace allowed between name and `(`; quoted names may be calls. `COUNT()`, `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, `f(a, b)`, `COUNT(t.*)` → ParseErrors at the offending token.
- `item`: `*` | `name . *` (3-token lookahead) | `expr [[AS] name]`; an alias without `AS` is any IDENT/QUOTED_IDENT token.
- `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take an INTEGER literal token only (`LIMIT -1`, `LIMIT 1.5` are ParseErrors); `OFFSET` without `LIMIT` is legal; `OFFSET … LIMIT …` is a ParseError at `LIMIT`. Optional single `;` then EOF.
- AST nodes record `start`/`end` (first to last character of the construct), a `pos` offset for error reporting (operator token for binary/unary/logical/comparison ops; the `LIKE`/`IN` keyword for `[NOT] LIKE`/`[NOT] IN` (D9); function-name token for calls; first token for column refs; the `*` token in calls; the ESCAPE string token), and a distinct `Paren(expr)` node whose span includes the parentheses (Domain Expert F1).

### 5.4 Data directory and CSV loading (R2, R3)
- `connect(DIR)`: if `DIR` is missing or not a directory → `DataIOError("data directory not found: DIR")` immediately (DIR as given, `str(os.fspath(DIR))`).
- Table discovery: fresh `os.scandir` on every `execute`/`tables()`; a table is an entry with `entry.is_file()` (follows symlinks; excludes directories, FIFOs, broken links) whose name ends with `.csv` case-insensitively; stem = `name[:-4]` (D12). Lookup is case-insensitive (`str.lower()`); two stems equal case-insensitively → `ambiguous table file '<name>'` (name as written in the query) for any reference.
- Read with `open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='')` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)`, streaming as the contract literally states (D5). Only tables referenced in FROM/JOIN are read, in FROM order, during semantic analysis.
- Records with zero fields (blank lines, before or after the header) are skipped. The first non-empty record is the header; no header → `<file>: empty file` (empty file, BOM-only, blank-lines-only).
- Header: names used verbatim; empty name → `<file>: empty column name`; duplicate names (case-insensitive) → `<file>: duplicate column 'C'` with `C` the second occurrence as written.
- Field-count mismatch → `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M` with N = `reader.line_num` after that record. `csv.Error` → `<file>: line N: malformed CSV` with N = `line_num` when raised. `UnicodeDecodeError` → `<file>: invalid UTF-8`. Other `OSError` while opening/reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` (D13; no contract template, defensive only).
- `<file>` is the base file name as on disk.
- Type inference per column over non-empty raw fields (no trimming) using `re.fullmatch` with explicit ASCII classes: all match `[+-]?[0-9]+` → INTEGER (`int`); else all match `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` → REAL (`float`); else TEXT (verbatim). No non-empty fields → TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. `re.fullmatch` is required (`re.match(...$)` would accept a trailing `\n`) (Codebase Analyst §3.35).
- `tables()` lists stems sorted by `(s.lower(), s)` without reading contents; ambiguous stems are both listed (D14). `schema(table)` loads the table (with IO errors as above) and returns `[(column, type)]` in header order; unknown table → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 (D15).

### 5.5 Name resolution and output names (R6, R10)
- Range name of a tableref = alias if present, else table name; a table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier (`emp.id` with `FROM emp e` → `unknown column 'emp.id'`). Duplicate range names (case-insensitive) → `duplicate table name 'N'` at the second tableref's range-name token.
- Unqualified `c` searches all FROM tables; `q.c` searches range `q`; zero matches → `unknown column 'R'`, more than one → `ambiguous column 'R'`, at the column-ref start. ON sees only tables introduced before or in its own join. Joins associate left. All name matching is case-insensitive.
- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in FROM order; `t.*` to that table's columns; unknown/hidden `t` → `unknown table 't'` at the `t` token (D10). `SELECT *` without FROM expands to zero columns (D11).
- Output name: alias as written (quotes removed, `""` → `"`); else for an unparenthesized column reference (qualified or not), the column's header name from the CSV; else verbatim source text `sql[item.start:item.end]` (keeps inner whitespace/comments/newlines; e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).

### 5.6 Static typing (R7)
- Types: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, NULL (bare `NULL` literal only, plus results derived per rules below). LEFT JOIN does not change a column's static type (D2).
- Arithmetic `+ - * / %`: operands INTEGER/REAL/NULL else `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2` at the operator. Result REAL if either REAL; else NULL if both NULL; else INTEGER. Unary `-`/`+`: operand numeric/NULL else `cannot apply 'OP' to T`; result keeps operand type.
- Comparisons and each `IN` item vs `x`: both numeric, both TEXT, or either NULL; else two-type mismatch (OP as written; `IN` for IN). Result INTEGER.
- `LIKE`: both operands TEXT or NULL, else `cannot apply 'LIKE' to T1 and T2` at the `LIKE` token; `ESCAPE` string must be exactly one code point else `ESCAPE must be a single character` at the ESCAPE string. Result INTEGER.
- `IS [NOT] NULL`: any operand; INTEGER.
- `AND`/`OR`: operands numeric/NULL else two-type mismatch (`AND`/`OR`); `NOT`: single-type mismatch (`NOT`). Results INTEGER.
- `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` condition of type TEXT → `condition must be numeric, got TEXT` at the condition expression's start (first character, e.g. `(` for `WHERE (name)`). Checks run bottom-up, so inner operator mismatches are reported first.
- Aggregates: `COUNT(*)`/`COUNT(e)` → INTEGER (any type). `SUM`: INTEGER→INTEGER, REAL→REAL, NULL→NULL (D4), TEXT → `cannot apply 'SUM' to TEXT` at the function name. `AVG`: numeric/NULL → REAL, TEXT → `cannot apply 'AVG' to TEXT`. `MIN`/`MAX`: any type, keeps argument type. Non-COUNT `X(*)` → `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT` at the `*`. Unknown name → `unknown function 'F'` at the name (checked before the `*` rule, D16).
- Result `types` list uses `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"`, `"NULL"`.

### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).

### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.
