1	"""Semantic analysis: table loading, name resolution, static typing, aggregate and ORDER BY rules."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from dataclasses import dataclass, fields, replace
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	from . import nodes as n
8	from .errors import SemanticError
9	from .plan import (
10	    AggSpec, BAggRef, BArith, BCol, BCompare, BGroupRef, BIn, BIsNull, BLike, BLit, BLogical,
11	    BNot, BoundQuery, BUnary, OrderSpec,
12	)
13	
14	_AGGREGATES = ("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max")
15	_ARITH = ("+", "-", "*", "/", "%")
16	_NUMERIC = ("INTEGER", "REAL", "NULL")
17	
18	
19	@dataclass
20	class _AggCall:
21	    """Aggregate call before the group-level rewrite (never reaches the executor)."""
22	    func: str
23	    arg: Any  # row-level bound expression or None for '*'
24	    type: str
25	    pos: int
26	
27	
28	_BOUND = (BCol, BLit, BUnary, BArith, BCompare, BLogical, BNot, BIsNull, BLike, BIn, _AggCall)
29	
30	
31	def analyze(query: n.Query, sql: str, catalog) -> BoundQuery:
32	    return _Analyzer(sql, catalog).run(query)
33	
34	
35	def _children(b):
36	    for f in fields(b):
37	        v = getattr(b, f.name)
38	        if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
39	            yield v
40	        elif isinstance(v, list):
41	            yield from v
42	
43	
44	def _has_agg(b):
45	    return isinstance(b, _AggCall) or any(_has_agg(c) for c in _children(b))
46	
47	
48	def _key(b):
49	    """Structural identity key (Paren already dropped; '<>' == '!='; literals by type and value)."""
50	    if isinstance(b, BLit):
51	        return ("lit", b.type, b.value)
52	    if isinstance(b, BCol):
53	        return ("col", b.index)
54	    parts = [type(b).__name__]
55	    for f in fields(b):
56	        if f.name in ("type", "pos"):
57	            continue
58	        v = getattr(b, f.name)
59	        if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
60	            v = _key(v)
61	        elif isinstance(v, list):
62	            v = tuple(_key(x) for x in v)
63	        elif f.name == "op" and v == "<>":
64	            v = "!="
65	        parts.append(v)
66	    return tuple(parts)
67	
68	
69	def _comparable(a, b):
70	    return "NULL" in (a, b) or (a == "TEXT") == (b == "TEXT")
71	
72	
73	class _Analyzer:
74	    def __init__(self, sql, catalog):
75	        self.sql = sql
76	        self.catalog = catalog
77	
78	    def error(self, offset, message):
79	        return SemanticError.at(self.sql, offset, message)
80	
81	    def mismatch(self, offset, op, *types):
82	        return self.error(offset, "type mismatch: cannot apply '%s' to %s" % (op, " and ".join(types)))
83	
84	    # ---- pass (a): resolve and type ----
85	
86	    def run(self, q):
87	        tables, offsets, scope, seen, width = [], [], [], set(), 0
88	        refs = [] if q.from_table is None else [q.from_table] + [j.table for j in q.joins]
89	        for ref in refs:
90	            table = self.catalog.load(ref.name)
91	            if table is None:
92	                raise self.error(ref.name_pos, "unknown table '%s'" % ref.name)
93	            if ref.range_name.lower() in seen:
94	                raise self.error(ref.range_pos, "duplicate table name '%s'" % ref.range_name)
95	            seen.add(ref.range_name.lower())
96	            tables.append(table)
97	            offsets.append(width)
98	            scope.append((ref.range_name, table, width))
99	            width += len(table.columns)
100	        headers = [c for t in tables for c in t.columns]
101	
102	        joins = [(j.kind, self.condition(j.on, scope[:i + 2], False)) for i, j in enumerate(q.joins)]
103	
104	        select, columns, entries, aliases = [], [], [], []
105	        for item in q.items:
106	            if isinstance(item, n.ExprItem):
107	                b = self.bind(item.expr, scope, True)
108	                if item.alias is not None:
109	                    name = item.alias
110	                    aliases.append((item.alias.lower(), len(select)))
111	                elif isinstance(item.expr, n.ColumnRef):
112	                    name = headers[b.index]
113	                else:
114	                    name = self.sql[item.start:item.end]
115	                entries.append(("expr", len(select)))
116	                select.append(b)
117	                columns.append(name)
118	                continue
119	            if isinstance(item, n.StarItem):
120	                expand, star_pos = scope, item.pos
121	            else:
122	                expand = [s for s in scope if s[0].lower() == item.qualifier.lower()]
123	                if not expand:
124	                    raise self.error(item.qualifier_pos, "unknown table '%s'" % item.qualifier)
125	                star_pos = item.star_pos
126	            entries.append(("star", star_pos))
127	            for _, table, off in expand:
128	                for i, col in enumerate(table.columns):
129	                    select.append(BCol(off + i, col, table.types[i], star_pos))
130	                    columns.append(col)
131	
132	        where = None if q.where is None else self.condition(q.where, scope, False)
133	        group_by = [self.bind(g, scope, False) for g in q.group_by]
134	        having = None if q.having is None else self.condition(q.having, scope, True)
135	
136	        order = []  # (OrderItem, output index or None, bound expr or None)
137	        for item in q.order_by:
138	            e = item.expr
139	            if isinstance(e, n.Literal) and e.kind == "INTEGER":
140	                if not 1 <= e.value <= len(select):
141	                    raise self.error(e.pos, "ORDER BY position %s is out of range" % e.value)
142	                order.append((item, e.value - 1, None))
143	                continue
144	            if isinstance(e, n.ColumnRef) and e.qualifier is None:
145	                hits = [i for a, i in aliases if a == e.name.lower()]
146	                if len(hits) > 1:
147	                    raise self.error(e.pos, "ambiguous column '%s'" % e.name)
148	                if hits:

152	
153	        # ---- pass (b): aggregate query, grouping, DISTINCT ----
154	        is_agg = (bool(group_by) or having is not None or any(_has_agg(b) for b in select)
155	                  or any(b is not None and _has_agg(b) for _, _, b in order))
156	        select_keys = [_key(b) for b in select]
157	        aggs, akeys, gkeys = [], {}, {}
158	        for i, g in enumerate(group_by):
159	            gkeys.setdefault(_key(g), i)
160	
161	        def group_level(b):
162	            """Rewrite to a group-level expression (BGroupRef / BAggRef / literals / operators)."""
163	            k = _key(b)
164	            if k in gkeys:
165	                return BGroupRef(gkeys[k], b.type, b.pos)
166	            if isinstance(b, _AggCall):
167	                if k not in akeys:
168	                    akeys[k] = len(aggs)
169	                    aggs.append(AggSpec(b.func, b.arg, b.type, b.pos))
170	                return BAggRef(akeys[k], b.type, b.pos)
171	            if isinstance(b, BLit):
172	                return b
173	            if isinstance(b, BCol):
174	                raise self.error(
175	                    b.pos, "column '%s' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate" % b.name)
176	            changes = {}
177	            for f in fields(b):
178	                v = getattr(b, f.name)
179	                if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
180	                    changes[f.name] = group_level(v)
181	                elif isinstance(v, list):
182	                    changes[f.name] = [group_level(x) for x in v]
183	            return replace(b, **changes)
184	
185	        if is_agg:
186	            for kind, val in entries:
187	                if kind == "star":
188	                    raise self.error(val, "'*' not allowed in aggregate query")
189	                select[val] = group_level(select[val])
190	            if having is not None:
191	                having = group_level(having)
192	
193	        specs = []
194	        for item, index, b in order:
195	            if b is not None and q.distinct:
196	                k = _key(b)
197	                if k not in select_keys:
198	                    raise self.error(
199	                        item.expr.start, "ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used")
200	                index = select_keys.index(k)
201	            if index is not None:
202	                specs.append(OrderSpec("output", index, None, item.desc))
203	            else:
204	                specs.append(OrderSpec("expr", None, group_level(b) if is_agg else b, item.desc))
205	
206	        return BoundQuery(tables, offsets, joins, where, is_agg, group_by, aggs, having, select,
207	                          columns, [b.type for b in select], specs, q.distinct, q.limit, q.offset)
208	
209	    def condition(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
210	        b = self.bind(e, scope, agg_ok)
211	        if b.type == "TEXT":
212	            raise self.error(e.start, "condition must be numeric, got TEXT")
213	        return b
214	
215	    def column(self, e, scope):
216	        if e.qualifier is None:
217	            ref, cands = e.name, scope
218	        else:
219	            ref = "%s.%s" % (e.qualifier, e.name)
220	            cands = [s for s in scope if s[0].lower() == e.qualifier.lower()]
221	        matches = [(t, off, i) for _, t, off in cands
222	                   for i, c in enumerate(t.columns) if c.lower() == e.name.lower()]
223	        if not matches:
224	            raise self.error(e.pos, "unknown column '%s'" % ref)
225	        if len(matches) > 1:
226	            raise self.error(e.pos, "ambiguous column '%s'" % ref)
227	        t, off, i = matches[0]
228	        return BCol(off + i, ref, t.types[i], e.pos)
229	
230	    def bind(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
231	        """Bottom-up: children are bound (and checked) before the node itself."""
232	        if isinstance(e, n.Paren):
233	            return self.bind(e.expr, scope, agg_ok)
234	        if isinstance(e, n.Literal):
235	            return BLit(e.value, e.kind, e.pos)
236	        if isinstance(e, n.ColumnRef):
237	            return self.column(e, scope)
238	        if isinstance(e, n.Call):
239	            return self.call(e, scope, agg_ok)
240	        if isinstance(e, (n.Unary, n.Not)):
241	            x = self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok)
242	            op = "NOT" if isinstance(e, n.Not) else e.op
243	            if x.type not in _NUMERIC:
244	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, op, x.type)
245	            if isinstance(e, n.Not):
246	                return BNot(x, "INTEGER", e.pos)
247	            return BUnary(e.op, x, x.type, e.pos)
248	        if isinstance(e, n.IsNull):
249	            return BIsNull(self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok), e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
250	        if isinstance(e, n.InList):
251	            x = self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok)
252	            items = [self.bind(i, scope, agg_ok) for i in e.items]
253	            for i in items:
254	                if not _comparable(x.type, i.type):
255	                    raise self.mismatch(e.pos, "IN", x.type, i.type)
256	            return BIn(x, items, e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
257	        left = self.bind(e.operand if isinstance(e, n.Like) else e.left, scope, agg_ok)
258	        right = self.bind(e.pattern if isinstance(e, n.Like) else e.right, scope, agg_ok)
259	        types = (left.type, right.type)
260	        if isinstance(e, n.Like):
261	            if not set(types) <= {"TEXT", "NULL"}:
262	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, "LIKE", *types)
263	            escape = None
264	            if e.escape is not None:
265	                escape = e.escape.value
266	                if len(escape) != 1:
267	                    raise self.error(e.escape.pos, "ESCAPE must be a single character")
268	            return BLike(left, right, escape, e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
269	        if isinstance(e, n.Logical) or e.op in _ARITH:
270	            if left.type not in _NUMERIC or right.type not in _NUMERIC:
271	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, e.op, *types)
272	            if isinstance(e, n.Logical):
273	                return BLogical(e.op, left, right, "INTEGER", e.pos)
274	            t = "REAL" if "REAL" in types else "NULL" if types == ("NULL", "NULL") else "INTEGER"
275	            return BArith(e.op, left, right, t == "REAL", t, e.pos)
276	        if not _comparable(*types):
277	            raise self.mismatch(e.pos, e.op, *types)
278	        return BCompare(e.op, left, right, "INTEGER", e.pos)
279	
280	    def call(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
281	        if e.name.lower() not in _AGGREGATES:
282	            raise self.error(e.pos, "unknown function '%s'" % e.name)
283	        func = e.name.lower().upper()
284	        if e.star and func != "COUNT":
285	            raise self.error(e.star_pos, "'*' argument only allowed for COUNT")
286	        if not agg_ok:
287	            raise self.error(e.pos, "aggregate function not allowed here")
288	        arg = None if e.star else self.bind(e.arg, scope, False)
289	        if func == "COUNT":
290	            t = "INTEGER"
291	        elif func in ("SUM", "AVG"):
292	            if arg.type == "TEXT":
293	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, func, "TEXT")
294	            t = "REAL" if func == "AVG" else arg.type
295	        else:
296	            t = arg.type
297	        return _AggCall(func, arg, t, e.pos)

1	# minisql: Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- Stack: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- Package location: `minisql/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`), with `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`.
7	- Entry points: `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` from repo root; `import minisql; minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
8	- Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser.
9	
10	## Functional requirements
11	
12	- **R1** Importable as `minisql`, runnable as `python -m minisql`; standard-library imports only, never `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser.
13	- **R2** Tables load from the data directory per the data contract.
14	- **R3** Column types are inferred per the inference rules; empty fields are NULL.
15	- **R4** The tokenizer implements the lexical rules.
16	- **R5** The parser implements the grammar and precedence table.
17	- **R6** Keywords and all names resolve case-insensitively.
18	- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
19	- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
20	- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
21	- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.
22	- **R11** INNER and LEFT joins follow nested-loop semantics and order.
23	- **R12** Grouping, `HAVING` and aggregates follow the aggregate rules, including empty input.
24	- **R13** `DISTINCT` keeps first occurrences.
25	- **R14** `ORDER BY` supports aliases, ordinals, expressions, multiple keys, `ASC`/`DESC`; NULLs smallest; stable ties.
26	- **R15** `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take non-negative integer literals.
27	- **R16** Clauses evaluate in the defined order; `AND`/`OR` short-circuit.
28	- **R17** The library API matches the contract.
29	- **R18** CSV and table formats match byte-for-byte.
30	- **R19** The one-shot CLI follows the output and exit-code rules.
31	- **R20** The REPL follows the prompt, buffering, command and exit rules.
32	- **R21** Errors use the specified classes, format, templates and positions.
33	
34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
44	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.
45	
46	### Grammar (EBNF)
47	
48	```
49	query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
50	            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
51	            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
54	item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
55	tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
63	                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
64	cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
65	add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
66	mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
67	unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
68	primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
69	call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
70	colref    = name ["." name] ;
71	name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
72	```
73	
74	`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.
75	
76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |
87	
88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
123	
124	### Aggregates and grouping
125	
126	- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
127	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
128	- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
129	- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.
130	
131	### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT
132	
133	- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
134	- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
135	- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
136	- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.
137	
138	### Evaluation order
139	
140	1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
141	2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.
142	
143	`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.
144	
145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.
190	
191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.
206	
207	## Acceptance criteria
208	
209	Fixture `emp.csv`: `id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`. Fixture `dept.csv`: `code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`.
210	
211	- **AC1** (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
212	- **AC2** (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
213	- **AC3** (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
214	- **AC4** (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
215	- **AC5** (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
216	- **AC6** (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann` (header from the CSV, not the query).
217	- **AC7** (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
218	- **AC8** (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
219	- **AC9** (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
220	- **AC10** (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
221	- **AC11** (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
222	- **AC12** (R2-R21) Behaviour specified in the Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections is reproduced exactly (byte-for-byte output, exit codes and error lines) by hidden tests.

1	"""Command-line entry point: one-shot query or REPL; exit codes 0/1/2/3, never a traceback."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import argparse
5	import os
6	import sys
7	from typing import List, Optional
8	
9	from .api import connect
10	from .errors import MiniSQLError
11	from .formatting import format_csv, format_table
12	
13	
14	def _setup_streams() -> None:
15	    """D18: UTF-8 with '\\n' on every platform, whatever PYTHONIOENCODING says."""
16	    for stream, errors in ((sys.stdout, "backslashreplace"), (sys.stderr, "backslashreplace"),
17	                           (sys.stdin, "replace")):
18	        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
19	            try:
20	                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=errors, newline="\n")
21	            except Exception:  # replaced/closed streams (e.g. under test harnesses)
22	                pass
23	
24	
25	def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
26	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="minisql", allow_abbrev=False)
27	    p.add_argument("--data", default=".", metavar="DIR", help="directory of CSV tables (default: .)")
28	    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["csv", "table"], default=None,
29	                   help="output format (one-shot default: csv; REPL default: table)")
30	    p.add_argument("sql", nargs="?", default=None, metavar="SQL", help="query to run; omit for the REPL")
31	    return p
32	
33	
34	def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
35	    try:
36	        conn = connect(args.data)
37	        if args.sql is None:
38	            from .repl import run_repl
39	            return run_repl(conn, args.format or "table", sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr)
40	        result = conn.execute(args.sql)
41	        text = format_table(result) if args.format == "table" else format_csv(result)
42	    except MiniSQLError as err:
43	        sys.stderr.write(str(err) + "\n")
44	        sys.stderr.flush()
45	        return 3 if err.kind == "IO" else 1
46	    sys.stdout.write(text)
47	    sys.stdout.flush()
48	    return 0
49	
50	
51	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
52	    _setup_streams()
53	    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)  # usage errors: SystemExit(2) propagates
54	    try:
55	        return _run(args)
56	    except BrokenPipeError:
57	        try:
58	            os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())
59	        except Exception:
60	            pass
61	        return 1
62	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
63	        return 130
64	    except Exception as exc:  # D19: one RuntimeError line, never a traceback
65	        try:
66	            sys.stderr.write("RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s\n" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))
67	            sys.stderr.flush()
68	        except Exception:
69	            pass
70	        return 1
71

1	"""Interactive REPL: prompts, statement buffering, dot-commands; exit 0 at EOF or .quit (R20)."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import re
5	
6	from .errors import MiniSQLError
7	from .formatting import format_csv, format_table
8	
9	PROMPT = "minisql> "
10	CONTINUATION = "   ...> "
11	_WS = " \t\r\n"
12	
13	HELP = (
14	    "Enter SQL statements terminated by ';'.\n"
15	    "Commands:\n"
16	    "  .help                 show this help\n"
17	    "  .tables               list tables\n"
18	    "  .schema NAME          show columns of table NAME\n"
19	    "  .format csv|table     set output format\n"
20	    "  .quit, .exit          leave the REPL\n"
21	)
22	
23	
24	def _error(stdout, stderr, text: str) -> None:
25	    stdout.flush()
26	    stderr.write(text + "\n")
27	    stderr.flush()
28	
29	
30	def _guarded(stdout, stderr, action) -> None:
31	    """Run `action()`; MiniSQLError / unexpected errors become one stderr line (D19)."""
32	    try:
33	        action()
34	    except MiniSQLError as err:
35	        _error(stdout, stderr, str(err))
36	    except Exception as exc:
37	        _error(stdout, stderr, "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))
38	
39	
40	def run_repl(conn, fmt: str, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int:
41	    state = {"fmt": fmt}
42	    buffer = None  # None = empty buffer; otherwise the accumulated text
43	
44	    def write(text: str) -> None:
45	        stdout.write(text)
46	        stdout.flush()
47	
48	    def execute(sql: str) -> None:
49	        result = conn.execute(sql)
50	        write(format_csv(result) if state["fmt"] == "csv" else format_table(result))
51	
52	    def schema(name: str) -> None:
53	        write("".join("%s %s\n" % col for col in conn.schema(name)))
54	
55	    def command(stripped: str) -> bool:
56	        """Run a dot-command; return True when the REPL should exit."""
57	        parts = re.split(r"[ \t]+", stripped)
58	        word, args = parts[0], parts[1:]
59	        if word in (".quit", ".exit") and not args:
60	            return True
61	        if word == ".help" and not args:
62	            write(HELP)
63	        elif word == ".tables" and not args:
64	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: write("".join(t + "\n" for t in conn.tables())))
65	        elif word == ".schema" and len(args) == 1:
66	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: schema(args[0]))
67	        elif word == ".format" and len(args) == 1 and args[0] in ("csv", "table"):
68	            state["fmt"] = args[0]
69	        else:
70	            _error(stdout, stderr, "unknown command: " + stripped)
71	        return False
72	
73	    while True:
74	        write(PROMPT if buffer is None else CONTINUATION)
75	        line = stdin.readline()
76	        if line == "":
77	            if buffer is not None:
78	                _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: execute(buffer))
79	            return 0
80	        if line.endswith("\n"):
81	            line = line[:-1]
82	        if buffer is None:
83	            stripped = line.strip(_WS)
84	            if not stripped:
85	                continue
86	            if stripped.startswith("."):
87	                if command(stripped):
88	                    return 0
89	                continue
90	            buffer = line
91	        else:
92	            buffer += "\n" + line
93	        if buffer.rstrip(_WS).endswith(";"):
94	            sql, buffer = buffer, None
95	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: execute(sql))
96

1	"""CSV and table output formatting (contract: Output formats)."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Optional
5	
6	from .result import Result
7	
8	_NUMERIC = ("INTEGER", "REAL")
9	
10	
11	def value_text(v, type_: str) -> Optional[str]:
12	    """Text of a value, chosen by its Python type; None for NULL. `type_` is informational."""
13	    if v is None:
14	        return None
15	    if isinstance(v, float):
16	        return repr(v)
17	    if isinstance(v, int):
18	        return str(v)
19	    return v
20	
21	
22	def _csv_field(text: Optional[str]) -> str:
23	    if text is None:
24	        return ""
25	    if (
26	        text == ""
27	        or any(c in text for c in ',"\n\r')
28	        or text.startswith(" ")
29	        or text.endswith(" ")
30	    ):
31	        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
32	    return text
33	
34	
35	def format_csv(result: Result) -> str:
36	    lines = [",".join(_csv_field(name) for name in result.columns)]
37	    for row in result.rows:
38	        lines.append(
39	            ",".join(_csv_field(value_text(v, t)) for v, t in zip(row, result.types))
40	        )
41	    return "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)
42	
43	
44	def _escape(text: str) -> str:
45	    return text.replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r")
46	
47	
48	def format_table(result: Result) -> str:
49	    headers = [_escape(name) for name in result.columns]
50	    body = []
51	    for row in result.rows:
52	        cells = []
53	        for v, t in zip(row, result.types):
54	            text = value_text(v, t)
55	            cells.append((_escape(text), t in _NUMERIC) if text is not None else ("NULL", False))
56	        body.append(cells)
57	    widths = [len(h) for h in headers]
58	    for cells in body:
59	        for i, (text, _) in enumerate(cells):
60	            widths[i] = max(widths[i], len(text))
61	    lines = [
62	        " | ".join(h.ljust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, widths)),
63	        "-+-".join("-" * w for w in widths),
64	    ]
65	    for cells in body:
66	        lines.append(
67	            " | ".join(
68	                text.rjust(w) if right else text.ljust(w)
69	                for (text, right), w in zip(cells, widths)
70	            )
71	        )
72	    n = len(result.rows)
73	    lines = [line.rstrip(" ") for line in lines]
74	    lines.append("(1 row)" if n == 1 else "(%d rows)" % n)
75	    return "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)

1	"""Error hierarchy and position helper shared by every minisql phase."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Optional, Tuple
5	
6	
7	def line_col(sql: str, offset: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
8	    """1-based (line, column) for a code-point offset; lines split on '\\n' only."""
9	    line = sql.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
10	    column = offset - (sql.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1) + 1
11	    return line, column
12	
13	
14	class MiniSQLError(Exception):
15	    kind = ""
16	
17	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: Optional[int] = None, column: Optional[int] = None):
18	        self.message = message
19	        self.line = line
20	        self.column = column
21	        super().__init__(self._format())
22	
23	    def _format(self) -> str:
24	        if self.kind == "IO":
25	            return "IOError: %s" % self.message
26	        return "%sError at line %s, column %s: %s" % (self.kind, self.line, self.column, self.message)
27	
28	    def __str__(self) -> str:
29	        return self._format()
30	
31	    @classmethod
32	    def at(cls, sql: str, offset: int, message: str) -> "MiniSQLError":
33	        line, column = line_col(sql, offset)
34	        return cls(message, line, column)
35	
36	
37	class LexError(MiniSQLError):
38	    kind = "Lex"
39	
40	
41	class ParseError(MiniSQLError):
42	    kind = "Parse"
43	
44	
45	class SemanticError(MiniSQLError):
46	    kind = "Semantic"
47	
48	
49	class QueryRuntimeError(MiniSQLError):
50	    kind = "Runtime"
51	
52	
53	class DataIOError(MiniSQLError):
54	    kind = "IO"

1	"""Semantic analysis: table loading, name resolution, static typing, aggregate and ORDER BY rules."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from dataclasses import dataclass, fields, replace
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	from . import nodes as n
8	from .errors import SemanticError
9	from .plan import (
10	    AggSpec, BAggRef, BArith, BCol, BCompare, BGroupRef, BIn, BIsNull, BLike, BLit, BLogical,
11	    BNot, BoundQuery, BUnary, OrderSpec,
12	)
13	
14	_AGGREGATES = ("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max")
15	_ARITH = ("+", "-", "*", "/", "%")
16	_NUMERIC = ("INTEGER", "REAL", "NULL")
17	
18	
19	@dataclass
20	class _AggCall:
21	    """Aggregate call before the group-level rewrite (never reaches the executor)."""
22	    func: str
23	    arg: Any  # row-level bound expression or None for '*'
24	    type: str
25	    pos: int
26	
27	
28	_BOUND = (BCol, BLit, BUnary, BArith, BCompare, BLogical, BNot, BIsNull, BLike, BIn, _AggCall)
29	
30	
31	def analyze(query: n.Query, sql: str, catalog) -> BoundQuery:
32	    return _Analyzer(sql, catalog).run(query)
33	
34	
35	def _children(b):
36	    for f in fields(b):
37	        v = getattr(b, f.name)
38	        if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
39	            yield v
40	        elif isinstance(v, list):
41	            yield from v
42	
43	
44	def _has_agg(b):
45	    return isinstance(b, _AggCall) or any(_has_agg(c) for c in _children(b))
46	
47	
48	def _key(b):
49	    """Structural identity key (Paren already dropped; '<>' == '!='; literals by type and value)."""
50	    if isinstance(b, BLit):
51	        return ("lit", b.type, b.value)
52	    if isinstance(b, BCol):
53	        return ("col", b.index)
54	    parts = [type(b).__name__]
55	    for f in fields(b):
56	        if f.name in ("type", "pos"):
57	            continue
58	        v = getattr(b, f.name)
59	        if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
60	            v = _key(v)
61	        elif isinstance(v, list):
62	            v = tuple(_key(x) for x in v)
63	        elif f.name == "op" and v == "<>":
64	            v = "!="
65	        parts.append(v)
66	    return tuple(parts)
67	
68	
69	def _comparable(a, b):
70	    return "NULL" in (a, b) or (a == "TEXT") == (b == "TEXT")
71	
72	
73	class _Analyzer:
74	    def __init__(self, sql, catalog):
75	        self.sql = sql
76	        self.catalog = catalog
77	
78	    def error(self, offset, message):
79	        return SemanticError.at(self.sql, offset, message)
80	
81	    def mismatch(self, offset, op, *types):
82	        return self.error(offset, "type mismatch: cannot apply '%s' to %s" % (op, " and ".join(types)))
83	
84	    # ---- pass (a): resolve and type ----
85	
86	    def run(self, q):
87	        tables, offsets, scope, seen, width = [], [], [], set(), 0
88	        refs = [] if q.from_table is None else [q.from_table] + [j.table for j in q.joins]
89	        for ref in refs:
90	            table = self.catalog.load(ref.name)
91	            if table is None:
92	                raise self.error(ref.name_pos, "unknown table '%s'" % ref.name)
93	            if ref.range_name.lower() in seen:
94	                raise self.error(ref.range_pos, "duplicate table name '%s'" % ref.range_name)
95	            seen.add(ref.range_name.lower())
96	            tables.append(table)
97	            offsets.append(width)
98	            scope.append((ref.range_name, table, width))
99	            width += len(table.columns)
100	        headers = [c for t in tables for c in t.columns]
101	
102	        joins = [(j.kind, self.condition(j.on, scope[:i + 2], False)) for i, j in enumerate(q.joins)]
103	
104	        select, columns, entries, aliases = [], [], [], []
105	        for item in q.items:
106	            if isinstance(item, n.ExprItem):
107	                b = self.bind(item.expr, scope, True)
108	                if item.alias is not None:
109	                    name = item.alias
110	                    aliases.append((item.alias.lower(), len(select)))
111	                elif isinstance(item.expr, n.ColumnRef):
112	                    name = headers[b.index]
113	                else:
114	                    name = self.sql[item.start:item.end]
115	                entries.append(("expr", len(select)))
116	                select.append(b)
117	                columns.append(name)
118	                continue
119	            if isinstance(item, n.StarItem):
120	                expand, star_pos = scope, item.pos
121	            else:
122	                expand = [s for s in scope if s[0].lower() == item.qualifier.lower()]
123	                if not expand:
124	                    raise self.error(item.qualifier_pos, "unknown table '%s'" % item.qualifier)
125	                star_pos = item.star_pos
126	            entries.append(("star", star_pos))
127	            for _, table, off in expand:
128	                for i, col in enumerate(table.columns):
129	                    select.append(BCol(off + i, col, table.types[i], star_pos))
130	                    columns.append(col)
131	
132	        where = None if q.where is None else self.condition(q.where, scope, False)
133	        group_by = [self.bind(g, scope, False) for g in q.group_by]
134	        having = None if q.having is None else self.condition(q.having, scope, True)
135	
136	        order = []  # (OrderItem, output index or None, bound expr or None)
137	        for item in q.order_by:
138	            e = item.expr
139	            if isinstance(e, n.Literal) and e.kind == "INTEGER":
140	                if not 1 <= e.value <= len(select):
141	                    raise self.error(e.pos, "ORDER BY position %s is out of range" % e.value)
142	                order.append((item, e.value - 1, None))
143	                continue
144	            if isinstance(e, n.ColumnRef) and e.qualifier is None:
145	                hits = [i for a, i in aliases if a == e.name.lower()]
146	                if len(hits) > 1:
147	                    raise self.error(e.pos, "ambiguous column '%s'" % e.name)
148	                if hits:
149	                    order.append((item, hits[0], None))
150	                    continue
151	            order.append((item, None, self.bind(e, scope, True)))
152	
153	        # ---- pass (b): aggregate query, grouping, DISTINCT ----
154	        is_agg = (bool(group_by) or having is not None or any(_has_agg(b) for b in select)
155	                  or any(b is not None and _has_agg(b) for _, _, b in order))
156	        select_keys = [_key(b) for b in select]
157	        aggs, akeys, gkeys = [], {}, {}
158	        for i, g in enumerate(group_by):
159	            gkeys.setdefault(_key(g), i)
160	
161	        def group_level(b):
162	            """Rewrite to a group-level expression (BGroupRef / BAggRef / literals / operators)."""
163	            k = _key(b)
164	            if k in gkeys:
165	                return BGroupRef(gkeys[k], b.type, b.pos)
166	            if isinstance(b, _AggCall):
167	                if k not in akeys:
168	                    akeys[k] = len(aggs)
169	                    aggs.append(AggSpec(b.func, b.arg, b.type, b.pos))
170	                return BAggRef(akeys[k], b.type, b.pos)
171	            if isinstance(b, BLit):
172	                return b
173	            if isinstance(b, BCol):
174	                raise self.error(
175	                    b.pos, "column '%s' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate" % b.name)
176	            changes = {}
177	            for f in fields(b):
178	                v = getattr(b, f.name)
179	                if isinstance(v, _BOUND):
180	                    changes[f.name] = group_level(v)
181	                elif isinstance(v, list):
182	                    changes[f.name] = [group_level(x) for x in v]
183	            return replace(b, **changes)
184	
185	        if is_agg:
186	            for kind, val in entries:
187	                if kind == "star":
188	                    raise self.error(val, "'*' not allowed in aggregate query")
189	                select[val] = group_level(select[val])
190	            if having is not None:
191	                having = group_level(having)
192	
193	        specs = []
194	        for item, index, b in order:
195	            if b is not None and q.distinct:
196	                k = _key(b)
197	                if k not in select_keys:
198	                    raise self.error(
199	                        item.expr.start, "ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used")
200	                index = select_keys.index(k)
201	            if index is not None:
202	                specs.append(OrderSpec("output", index, None, item.desc))
203	            else:
204	                specs.append(OrderSpec("expr", None, group_level(b) if is_agg else b, item.desc))
205	
206	        return BoundQuery(tables, offsets, joins, where, is_agg, group_by, aggs, having, select,
207	                          columns, [b.type for b in select], specs, q.distinct, q.limit, q.offset)
208	
209	    def condition(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
210	        b = self.bind(e, scope, agg_ok)
211	        if b.type == "TEXT":
212	            raise self.error(e.start, "condition must be numeric, got TEXT")
213	        return b
214	
215	    def column(self, e, scope):
216	        if e.qualifier is None:
217	            ref, cands = e.name, scope
218	        else:
219	            ref = "%s.%s" % (e.qualifier, e.name)
220	            cands = [s for s in scope if s[0].lower() == e.qualifier.lower()]
221	        matches = [(t, off, i) for _, t, off in cands
222	                   for i, c in enumerate(t.columns) if c.lower() == e.name.lower()]
223	        if not matches:
224	            raise self.error(e.pos, "unknown column '%s'" % ref)
225	        if len(matches) > 1:
226	            raise self.error(e.pos, "ambiguous column '%s'" % ref)
227	        t, off, i = matches[0]
228	        return BCol(off + i, ref, t.types[i], e.pos)
229	
230	    def bind(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
231	        """Bottom-up: children are bound (and checked) before the node itself."""
232	        if isinstance(e, n.Paren):
233	            return self.bind(e.expr, scope, agg_ok)
234	        if isinstance(e, n.Literal):
235	            return BLit(e.value, e.kind, e.pos)
236	        if isinstance(e, n.ColumnRef):
237	            return self.column(e, scope)
238	        if isinstance(e, n.Call):
239	            return self.call(e, scope, agg_ok)
240	        if isinstance(e, (n.Unary, n.Not)):
241	            x = self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok)
242	            op = "NOT" if isinstance(e, n.Not) else e.op
243	            if x.type not in _NUMERIC:
244	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, op, x.type)
245	            if isinstance(e, n.Not):
246	                return BNot(x, "INTEGER", e.pos)
247	            return BUnary(e.op, x, x.type, e.pos)
248	        if isinstance(e, n.IsNull):
249	            return BIsNull(self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok), e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
250	        if isinstance(e, n.InList):
251	            x = self.bind(e.operand, scope, agg_ok)
252	            items = [self.bind(i, scope, agg_ok) for i in e.items]
253	            for i in items:
254	                if not _comparable(x.type, i.type):
255	                    raise self.mismatch(e.pos, "IN", x.type, i.type)
256	            return BIn(x, items, e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
257	        left = self.bind(e.operand if isinstance(e, n.Like) else e.left, scope, agg_ok)
258	        right = self.bind(e.pattern if isinstance(e, n.Like) else e.right, scope, agg_ok)
259	        types = (left.type, right.type)
260	        if isinstance(e, n.Like):
261	            if not set(types) <= {"TEXT", "NULL"}:
262	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, "LIKE", *types)
263	            escape = None
264	            if e.escape is not None:
265	                escape = e.escape.value
266	                if len(escape) != 1:
267	                    raise self.error(e.escape.pos, "ESCAPE must be a single character")
268	            return BLike(left, right, escape, e.negated, "INTEGER", e.pos)
269	        if isinstance(e, n.Logical) or e.op in _ARITH:
270	            if left.type not in _NUMERIC or right.type not in _NUMERIC:
271	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, e.op, *types)
272	            if isinstance(e, n.Logical):
273	                return BLogical(e.op, left, right, "INTEGER", e.pos)
274	            t = "REAL" if "REAL" in types else "NULL" if types == ("NULL", "NULL") else "INTEGER"
275	            return BArith(e.op, left, right, t == "REAL", t, e.pos)
276	        if not _comparable(*types):
277	            raise self.mismatch(e.pos, e.op, *types)
278	        return BCompare(e.op, left, right, "INTEGER", e.pos)
279	
280	    def call(self, e, scope, agg_ok):
281	        if e.name.lower() not in _AGGREGATES:
282	            raise self.error(e.pos, "unknown function '%s'" % e.name)
283	        func = e.name.lower().upper()
284	        if e.star and func != "COUNT":
285	            raise self.error(e.star_pos, "'*' argument only allowed for COUNT")
286	        if not agg_ok:
287	            raise self.error(e.pos, "aggregate function not allowed here")
288	        arg = None if e.star else self.bind(e.arg, scope, False)
289	        if func == "COUNT":
290	            t = "INTEGER"
291	        elif func in ("SUM", "AVG"):
292	            if arg.type == "TEXT":
293	                raise self.mismatch(e.pos, func, "TEXT")
294	            t = "REAL" if func == "AVG" else arg.type
295	        else:
296	            t = arg.type
297	        return _AggCall(func, arg, t, e.pos)
298

1	"""Bound (resolved, statically typed) query plan: produced by analyzer.analyze, run by the executor.
2	
3	Every bound expression has `type` ('INTEGER' | 'REAL' | 'TEXT' | 'NULL') and `pos` (source offset;
4	for BArith the operator token, for BLike the LIKE token, which is where runtime errors are reported).
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	from dataclasses import dataclass
9	from typing import Any, List, Optional, Tuple
10	
11	# ---- row-level expressions -------------------------------------------------------
12	
13	
14	@dataclass
15	class BCol:
16	    index: int  # flat index into the joined row tuple
17	    name: str  # column reference as written ('c' or 'q.c'), diagnostics only
18	    type: str
19	    pos: int
20	
21	
22	@dataclass
23	class BLit:
24	    value: Any  # int | float | str | None
25	    type: str
26	    pos: int
27	
28	
29	@dataclass
30	class BUnary:
31	    op: str  # '-' | '+'
32	    operand: Any
33	    type: str  # operand type
34	    pos: int
35	
36	
37	@dataclass
38	class BArith:
39	    op: str  # '+' '-' '*' '/' '%'
40	    left: Any
41	    right: Any
42	    real: bool  # True iff type == 'REAL' (float semantics in evaluate.arith)
43	    type: str
44	    pos: int  # operator token
45	
46	
47	@dataclass
48	class BCompare:
49	    op: str  # '=' '<>' '!=' '<' '<=' '>' '>=' as written
50	    left: Any
51	    right: Any
52	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
53	    pos: int
54	
55	
56	@dataclass
57	class BLogical:
58	    op: str  # 'AND' | 'OR'
59	    left: Any
60	    right: Any
61	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
62	    pos: int
63	
64	
65	@dataclass
66	class BNot:
67	    operand: Any
68	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
69	    pos: int
70	
71	
72	@dataclass
73	class BIsNull:
74	    operand: Any
75	    negated: bool
76	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
77	    pos: int
78	
79	
80	@dataclass
81	class BLike:
82	    operand: Any
83	    pattern: Any
84	    escape: Optional[str]  # single character, or None without ESCAPE
85	    negated: bool
86	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
87	    pos: int  # LIKE token
88	
89	
90	@dataclass
91	class BIn:
92	    operand: Any
93	    items: List[Any]
94	    negated: bool
95	    type: str  # always 'INTEGER'
96	    pos: int
97	
98	
99	# ---- group-level references (aggregate queries only) -----------------------------
100	
101	
102	@dataclass
103	class BGroupRef:
104	    index: int  # group_key_values[index]
105	    type: str
106	    pos: int
107	
108	
109	@dataclass
110	class BAggRef:
111	    index: int  # aggregate_values[index], aggregate = BoundQuery.aggregates[index]
112	    type: str
113	    pos: int
114	
115	
116	# ---- query -----------------------------------------------------------------------
117	
118	
119	@dataclass
120	class AggSpec:
121	    func: str  # 'COUNT' | 'SUM' | 'AVG' | 'MIN' | 'MAX'
122	    arg: Any  # row-level bound expression, or None for COUNT(*)
123	    type: str  # result type
124	    pos: int  # function name token
125	
126	
127	@dataclass
128	class OrderSpec:
129	    kind: str  # 'output' | 'expr'
130	    index: Optional[int]  # 'output': 0-based position in the projected tuple
131	    expr: Any  # 'expr': row-level (plain query) or group-level (aggregate query) expression
132	    desc: bool
133	
134	
135	@dataclass
136	class BoundQuery:
137	    tables: List[Any]  # catalog.Table in FROM order; [] without FROM (one empty row)
138	    table_offsets: List[int]  # flat start index of each table's columns
139	    joins: List[Tuple[str, Any]]  # (kind 'INNER'|'LEFT', ON expr) joining tables[i + 1]
140	    where: Any  # row-level or None
141	    is_aggregate: bool
142	    group_by: List[Any]  # row-level
143	    aggregates: List[AggSpec]
144	    having: Any  # group-level or None
145	    select: List[Any]  # one per output column (after '*' expansion)
146	    columns: List[str]
147	    types: List[str]
148	    order: List[OrderSpec]
149	    distinct: bool
150	    limit: Optional[int]
151	    offset: Optional[int]

1	"""Error hierarchy and position helper shared by every minisql phase."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Optional, Tuple
5	
6	
7	def line_col(sql: str, offset: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
8	    """1-based (line, column) for a code-point offset; lines split on '\\n' only."""
9	    line = sql.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
10	    column = offset - (sql.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1) + 1
11	    return line, column
12	
13	
14	class MiniSQLError(Exception):
15	    kind = ""
16	
17	    def __init__(self, message: str, line: Optional[int] = None, column: Optional[int] = None):
18	        self.message = message
19	        self.line = line
20	        self.column = column
21	        super().__init__(self._format())
22	
23	    def _format(self) -> str:
24	        if self.kind == "IO":
25	            return "IOError: %s" % self.message
26	        return "%sError at line %s, column %s: %s" % (self.kind, self.line, self.column, self.message)
27	
28	    def __str__(self) -> str:
29	        return self._format()
30	
31	    @classmethod
32	    def at(cls, sql: str, offset: int, message: str) -> "MiniSQLError":
33	        line, column = line_col(sql, offset)
34	        return cls(message, line, column)
35	
36	
37	class LexError(MiniSQLError):
38	    kind = "Lex"
39	
40	
41	class ParseError(MiniSQLError):
42	    kind = "Parse"
43	
44	
45	class SemanticError(MiniSQLError):
46	    kind = "Semantic"
47	
48	
49	class QueryRuntimeError(MiniSQLError):
50	    kind = "Runtime"
51	
52	
53	class DataIOError(MiniSQLError):
54	    kind = "IO"

1	"""Stdlib-only guard: every import in minisql/*.py must be in the allowlist; never sqlite3."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import ast
5	import glob
6	import os
7	
8	REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
9	
10	# Explicit stdlib allowlist (do not use sys.stdlib_module_names; Python 3.9 lacks it).
11	# Tasks listing this file in scope may extend it with stdlib modules only.
12	STDLIB_ALLOWLIST = frozenset(
13	    """
14	    __future__ argparse codecs collections contextlib csv dataclasses decimal enum errno
15	    functools glob io itertools locale math numbers operator os pathlib re shutil signal
16	    stat string sys textwrap traceback types typing unicodedata warnings weakref
17	    """.split()
18	)
19	
20	
21	def _module_files():
22	    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "minisql", "*.py")))
23	    assert files, "no minisql/*.py files found"
24	    return files
25	
26	
27	def _imported_top_levels(path):
28	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
29	        tree = ast.parse(f.read(), filename=path)
30	    names = set()
31	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
32	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
33	            for alias in node.names:
34	                names.add(alias.name.split(".")[0])
35	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
36	            if node.level:  # relative import: within the package
37	                continue
38	            names.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
39	    return names
40	
41	
42	def test_only_stdlib_imports():
43	    bad = {}
44	    for path in _module_files():
45	        extra = _imported_top_levels(path) - STDLIB_ALLOWLIST - {"minisql"}
46	        if extra:
47	            bad[os.path.basename(path)] = sorted(extra)
48	    assert bad == {}
49	
50	
51	def test_no_sqlite3():
52	    assert "sqlite3" not in STDLIB_ALLOWLIST
53	    for path in _module_files():
54	        assert "sqlite3" not in _imported_top_levels(path), path

100	- AST nodes record `start`/`end` (first to last character of the construct), a `pos` offset for error reporting (operator token for binary/unary/logical/comparison ops; the `LIKE`/`IN` keyword for `[NOT] LIKE`/`[NOT] IN` (D9); function-name token for calls; first token for column refs; the `*` token in calls; the ESCAPE string token), and a distinct `Paren(expr)` node whose span includes the parentheses (Domain Expert F1).
101	
102	### 5.4 Data directory and CSV loading (R2, R3)
103	- `connect(DIR)`: if `DIR` is missing or not a directory → `DataIOError("data directory not found: DIR")` immediately (DIR as given, `str(os.fspath(DIR))`).
104	- Table discovery: fresh `os.scandir` on every `execute`/`tables()`; a table is an entry with `entry.is_file()` (follows symlinks; excludes directories, FIFOs, broken links) whose name ends with `.csv` case-insensitively; stem = `name[:-4]` (D12). Lookup is case-insensitive (`str.lower()`); two stems equal case-insensitively → `ambiguous table file '<name>'` (name as written in the query) for any reference.
105	- Read with `open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='')` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)`, streaming as the contract literally states (D5). Only tables referenced in FROM/JOIN are read, in FROM order, during semantic analysis.
106	- Records with zero fields (blank lines, before or after the header) are skipped. The first non-empty record is the header; no header → `<file>: empty file` (empty file, BOM-only, blank-lines-only).
107	- Header: names used verbatim; empty name → `<file>: empty column name`; duplicate names (case-insensitive) → `<file>: duplicate column 'C'` with `C` the second occurrence as written.
108	- Field-count mismatch → `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M` with N = `reader.line_num` after that record. `csv.Error` → `<file>: line N: malformed CSV` with N = `line_num` when raised. `UnicodeDecodeError` → `<file>: invalid UTF-8`. Other `OSError` while opening/reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` (D13; no contract template, defensive only).
109	- `<file>` is the base file name as on disk.
110	- Type inference per column over non-empty raw fields (no trimming) using `re.fullmatch` with explicit ASCII classes: all match `[+-]?[0-9]+` → INTEGER (`int`); else all match `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` → REAL (`float`); else TEXT (verbatim). No non-empty fields → TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. `re.fullmatch` is required (`re.match(...$)` would accept a trailing `\n`) (Codebase Analyst §3.35).
111	- `tables()` lists stems sorted by `(s.lower(), s)` without reading contents; ambiguous stems are both listed (D14). `schema(table)` loads the table (with IO errors as above) and returns `[(column, type)]` in header order; unknown table → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 (D15).
112	
113	### 5.5 Name resolution and output names (R6, R10)
114	- Range name of a tableref = alias if present, else table name; a table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier (`emp.id` with `FROM emp e` → `unknown column 'emp.id'`). Duplicate range names (case-insensitive) → `duplicate table name 'N'` at the second tableref's range-name token.
115	- Unqualified `c` searches all FROM tables; `q.c` searches range `q`; zero matches → `unknown column 'R'`, more than one → `ambiguous column 'R'`, at the column-ref start. ON sees only tables introduced before or in its own join. Joins associate left. All name matching is case-insensitive.
116	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in FROM order; `t.*` to that table's columns; unknown/hidden `t` → `unknown table 't'` at the `t` token (D10). `SELECT *` without FROM expands to zero columns (D11).
117	- Output name: alias as written (quotes removed, `""` → `"`); else for an unparenthesized column reference (qualified or not), the column's header name from the CSV; else verbatim source text `sql[item.start:item.end]` (keeps inner whitespace/comments/newlines; e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
118	
119	### 5.6 Static typing (R7)
120	- Types: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, NULL (bare `NULL` literal only, plus results derived per rules below). LEFT JOIN does not change a column's static type (D2).
121	- Arithmetic `+ - * / %`: operands INTEGER/REAL/NULL else `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2` at the operator. Result REAL if either REAL; else NULL if both NULL; else INTEGER. Unary `-`/`+`: operand numeric/NULL else `cannot apply 'OP' to T`; result keeps operand type.
122	- Comparisons and each `IN` item vs `x`: both numeric, both TEXT, or either NULL; else two-type mismatch (OP as written; `IN` for IN). Result INTEGER.
123	- `LIKE`: both operands TEXT or NULL, else `cannot apply 'LIKE' to T1 and T2` at the `LIKE` token; `ESCAPE` string must be exactly one code point else `ESCAPE must be a single character` at the ESCAPE string. Result INTEGER.
124	- `IS [NOT] NULL`: any operand; INTEGER.
125	- `AND`/`OR`: operands numeric/NULL else two-type mismatch (`AND`/`OR`); `NOT`: single-type mismatch (`NOT`). Results INTEGER.
126	- `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` condition of type TEXT → `condition must be numeric, got TEXT` at the condition expression's start (first character, e.g. `(` for `WHERE (name)`). Checks run bottom-up, so inner operator mismatches are reported first.
127	- Aggregates: `COUNT(*)`/`COUNT(e)` → INTEGER (any type). `SUM`: INTEGER→INTEGER, REAL→REAL, NULL→NULL (D4), TEXT → `cannot apply 'SUM' to TEXT` at the function name. `AVG`: numeric/NULL → REAL, TEXT → `cannot apply 'AVG' to TEXT`. `MIN`/`MAX`: any type, keeps argument type. Non-COUNT `X(*)` → `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT` at the `*`. Unknown name → `unknown function 'F'` at the name (checked before the `*` rule, D16).
128	- Result `types` list uses `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"`, `"NULL"`.
129	
130	### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
131	- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
132	- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
133	- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
134	- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
135	- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
136	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).
137	
138	### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
139	Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
140	1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
141	2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
142	- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
143	- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
144	- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
145	- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
146	- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
147	- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
148	- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
149	- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
150	- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
151	- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.
152

Importing `minisql` must not alter `sys.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None` (never `bool`).
165	
166	### 5.10 Output formats (R18)
167	- Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
168	- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
169	- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. A column of type NULL holds only NULL cells (left-aligned).
170	
171	### 5.11 CLI and REPL (R19, R20)
172	- `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`; argparse with `allow_abbrev=False`, `--data` default `.`, `--format` `choices=['csv','table']` default `None` (one-shot → csv, REPL → table), positional `sql` `nargs='?'`; `args.sql is not None` → one-shot (so `""` is one-shot with empty SQL). Usage errors: argparse exit 2.
173	- Stream setup in `cli.main()` only (never at import): `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='backslashreplace', newline='\n')`; `sys.stdin` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', newline='\n')` (Integration F11–F15; D18).
174	- One-shot: `connect` first (missing DIR → `IOError: …` exit 3 before lexing); execute; format the full output string, then write once. Errors: stdout empty, stderr exactly `str(err) + "\n"`; exit 1 for Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime, 3 for IO, 0 on success.
175	- Top-level guard: catch `MiniSQLError`; catch `BrokenPipeError` (redirect stdout to devnull, exit 1); `KeyboardInterrupt` (exit 130); any other unexpected `Exception` (e.g. `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`) → a single line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <exception text>` on stderr, exit 1 (D19) — never a traceback.
176	- REPL: prompt `minisql> ` when buffer empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces) otherwise, written to stdout without newline and flushed, regardless of TTY. Input not echoed. Read lines with `readline()`; strip one trailing `\n` only (keep `\r`; D18). With an empty buffer: a line whose stripped text (strip `' \t\r\n'`) starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise append the line (joined with `\n`); when the buffer right-stripped ends with `;`, execute it and clear the buffer.
177	- Commands (exact lower-case): `.help` (free text to stdout), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line; errors as one stderr line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit`, `.exit` (exit 0). Anything else (incl. `.format` with a bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).
178	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer. stdout is flushed before each stderr write.
179	- At EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. A missing `--data` DIR in REPL mode → `IOError: …` on stderr, exit 3 before the first prompt (D21).

181	### 5.12 Decision register
182	
183	Decisions taken where `contract.md` is silent or researchers diverged. Each picks the option closest to the contract text; the alternative is recorded.
184	
185	| ID | Decision | Alternative (rejected) | Basis |
186	|---|---|---|---|
187	| D1 | Code targets Python ≥ 3.11 but must also run on 3.9 (no `match`, no runtime PEP 604 unions, no 3.10+ stdlib APIs, `from __future__ import annotations`).
