188	| D2 | LEFT JOIN NULL-filled columns keep their inferred static type | Give them NULL type | "Any value may be None" |
189	| D3 | `types` entry `"NULL"` only for NULL-typed expressions (bare NULL, `-NULL`, `NULL+NULL`, `SUM/MIN/MAX(NULL)`); predicates over NULL are INTEGER | — | Contract type rules |
190	| D4 | `SUM(NULL)` → NULL type; `AVG(NULL)` → REAL; `MIN/MAX(NULL)` → NULL | Reject NULL-typed aggregate arguments | NULL type accepted wherever numeric is |
191	| D5 | CSV read by streaming `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` over the open file; first raised error wins | Decode whole file first so invalid UTF-8 always wins (Codebase Analyst A24) | Literal contract wording; oracle uses single-error files |
192	| D6 | `IN` does not short-circuit; `x` and all items evaluated left-to-right | Stop at first match | Only AND/OR are specified to short-circuit |
193	| D7 | LIKE: NULL operand checked before pattern validation → NULL | Validate pattern first | Mirrors "NULL … (checked first)" for arithmetic; "Any NULL operand gives NULL" |
194	| D8 | `<>` and `!=` structurally identical; literals identical by (type, value) | Textual identity | "same resolved columns, operators and literals" |
195	| D9 | `NOT LIKE`/`NOT IN` type errors use OP `LIKE`/`IN` at the `LIKE`/`IN` token | Position at `NOT` | Runtime LIKE errors are "at the `LIKE` token" |
196	| D10 | `q.*` with unknown/hidden `q` → `unknown table 'q'` at `q` | unknown column | Template list; table/name token |
197	| D11 | `SELECT *` without FROM → zero output columns, one row | SemanticError | Do not invent errors |
198	| D12 | Stem = `name[:-4]`; a file literally named `.csv` has stem `''` | `pathlib.Path.stem` | Contract "file stem" of `*.csv` |
199	| D13 | Non-decode OSError while reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` | Traceback | No-traceback rule; no template exists |
200	| D14 | `tables()` lists ambiguous stems (both) | Raise | "lists stems without reading file contents" |
201	| D15 | `schema(unknown)` → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 | DataIOError | Template exists only as Semantic |
202	| D16 | Unknown function reported before `'*'` argument rule | Reverse | Single-error oracle; name resolution precedes argument checks |
203	| D17 | Table format escapes `\n`/`\r` in header cells too | Escape only values | Preserves one-line rows |
204	| D18 | REPL stdin reconfigured to UTF-8 with `newline='\n'` (no CRLF translation; `\r` kept, lexer treats it as whitespace); stdin `errors='replace'` | Universal newlines (platform-dependent) | Byte-for-byte determinism across OSes |
205	| D19 | Unexpected internal exceptions (OverflowError, RecursionError) → one `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` line, exit 1; recursion limit raised modestly (e.g. 10000) in the parser/analyzer/evaluator entry | Traceback | "Never a traceback" |
206	| D20 | Malformed dot-commands → `unknown command: <stripped line>` | Separate usage messages | Only template given |
207	| D21 | REPL with missing DIR → IOError line, exit 3 | Start REPL anyway | `connect` raises immediately |
208	| D22 | `ambiguous table file 'N'`: N as written in the query (for `schema()`, the argument as given) | File stem | Contract N rule |

17	def connect(data_dir) -> "Connection":
18	    """`data_dir` is a str or os.PathLike; a missing or non-directory path raises DataIOError now."""

22	class Connection:
23	    def __init__(self, data_dir):
24	        self._catalog = Catalog(data_dir)
25	
26	    def execute(self, sql: str) -> Result:
27	        old = sys.getrecursionlimit()
28	        sys.setrecursionlimit(max(old, _RECURSION_LIMIT))
29	        try:
30	            return execute(analyze(parse(sql), sql, self._catalog), sql)
31	        except MiniSQLError:
32	            raise
33	        except Exception as exc:  # D19: RecursionError, OverflowError, int/str limits, ...
34	            raise QueryRuntimeError(str(exc) or type(exc).__name__, 1, 1) from None
35	        finally:
36	            sys.setrecursionlimit(old)
37	
38	    def tables(self) -> List[str]:
39	        return self._catalog.table_names()
40	
41	    def schema(self, table: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
42	        t = self._catalog.load(table)
43	        if t is None:
44	            raise SemanticError("unknown table '%s'" % table, 1, 1)
45	        return list(zip(t.columns, t.types))

72	## 5. Detailed Design
73	
74	Each subsection restates the governing contract rule and adds the binding design decisions. Decision IDs (Dn) are collected in §5.12.
75	
76	### 5.1 Errors and positions (R21)
77	- `MiniSQLError(Exception)` with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`. `str(err)` = `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO: `IOError: <message>`. Kind `Runtime` prints `RuntimeError at …` (class name `QueryRuntimeError`).
78	- All positions derive from an absolute code-point offset into the SQL text via one helper: `line = sql.count('\n', 0, off) + 1`; `column = off - (sql.rfind('\n', 0, off) + 1) + 1`. Lines split on `\n` only; tab and `\r` count as one column (Domain Expert F1).
79	- Message templates and positions exactly per the contract table (Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO). `N`, `R`, `F` as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`); `OP` as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates.
80	- Phase order: lex the whole input → parse fully → semantic (including IO for referenced tables in FROM order) → execute. All static errors are raised before any row is evaluated.
81	
82	### 5.2 Lexer (R4, R6)
83	- Whitespace exactly space, tab, `\r`, `\n`; anything else outside a token (e.g. NBSP, form feed, `#`, lone `!`) → `unexpected character 'X'` at that character.
84	- `--` comment to end of line (so `SELECT --1` is followed by EOF).
85	- Character classes are ASCII-only: identifiers `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; digits `[0-9]`. Never `str.isdigit/isalpha/isidentifier` or `\d` (Integration F25–26, Domain Expert F1).
86	- Keywords (case-insensitive, reserved): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`. Function names are identifiers.
87	- Quoted identifier `"..."` (`""` → `"`), may contain anything incl. newlines, may equal a keyword; unterminated → `unterminated quoted identifier` at the opening quote.
88	- String `'...'` (`''` → `'`), may span lines, backslash literal; unterminated → `unterminated string literal` at opening quote.
89	- Numbers: INTEGER `[0-9]+`; REAL `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` | `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. Longest match of these forms; if the next character is an ASCII letter, digit, `_` or `.` → `invalid number literal` at the literal start. Thus `12abc`, `1e`, `1e+`, `1..2`, `1.2.3`, `1_0`, `1.5e` are errors; `1.`, `1.e5`, `.5` are valid; `.` not followed by a digit is the `.` operator. REAL value = `float(text)`, INTEGER value = `int(text)`.
90	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . ;` and `*`.
91	- Each token carries `kind`, `value`, `text = sql[start:end]`, `start`, `end`. An EOF token sits at offset `len(sql)` ("one past last input character").
92	
93	### 5.3 Parser (R5)
94	- Recursive descent over the contract EBNF. Level 4 (comparison / IS / LIKE / IN) is non-associative: `cmp` parses at most one tail; a second comparison operator surfaces as `unexpected token '<text>'` at that operator (`a = b = c`, `a IS NULL IS NULL`).
95	- `NOT` binds looser than comparison (`NOT 1 = 2` = `NOT (1 = 2)` → 1); `1 = NOT 2` → ParseError at `NOT`.
96	- `unexpected token 'T'` uses the token's exact source text (strings keep their quotes, keywords keep written case). At EOF: `unexpected end of input` at offset `len(sql)`.
97	- Calls: `name "(" ("*" | expr) ")"`; whitespace allowed between name and `(`; quoted names may be calls. `COUNT()`, `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`, `f(a, b)`, `COUNT(t.*)` → ParseErrors at the offending token.
98	- `item`: `*` | `name . *` (3-token lookahead) | `expr [[AS] name]`; an alias without `AS` is any IDENT/QUOTED_IDENT token.
99	- `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take an INTEGER literal token only (`LIMIT -1`, `LIMIT 1.5` are ParseErrors); `OFFSET` without `LIMIT` is legal; `OFFSET … LIMIT …` is a ParseError at `LIMIT`. Optional single `;` then EOF.
100	- AST nodes record `start`/`end` (first to last character of the construct), a `pos` offset for error reporting (operator token for binary/unary/logical/comparison ops; the `LIKE`/`IN` keyword for `[NOT] LIKE`/`[NOT] IN` (D9); function-name token for calls; first token for column refs; the `*` token in calls; the ESCAPE string token), and a distinct `Paren(expr)` node whose span includes the parentheses (Domain Expert F1).
101	
102	### 5.4 Data directory and CSV loading (R2, R3)
103	- `connect(DIR)`: if `DIR` is missing or not a directory → `DataIOError("data directory not found: DIR")` immediately (DIR as given, `str(os.fspath(DIR))`).
104	- Table discovery: fresh `os.scandir` on every `execute`/`tables()`; a table is an entry with `entry.is_file()` (follows symlinks; excludes directories, FIFOs, broken links) whose name ends with `.csv` case-insensitively; stem = `name[:-4]` (D12). Lookup is case-insensitive (`str.lower()`); two stems equal case-insensitively → `ambiguous table file '<name>'` (name as written in the query) for any reference.
105	- Read with `open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='')` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)`, streaming as the contract literally states (D5). Only tables referenced in FROM/JOIN are read, in FROM order, during semantic analysis.
106	- Records with zero fields (blank lines, before or after the header) are skipped. The first non-empty record is the header; no header → `<file>: empty file` (empty file, BOM-only, blank-lines-only).
107	- Header: names used verbatim; empty name → `<file>: empty column name`; duplicate names (case-insensitive) → `<file>: duplicate column 'C'` with `C` the second occurrence as written.
108	- Field-count mismatch → `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M` with N = `reader.line_num` after that record. `csv.Error` → `<file>: line N: malformed CSV` with N = `line_num` when raised. `UnicodeDecodeError` → `<file>: invalid UTF-8`. Other `OSError` while opening/reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` (D13; no contract template, defensive only).
109	- `<file>` is the base file name as on disk.
110	- Type inference per column over non-empty raw fields (no trimming) using `re.fullmatch` with explicit ASCII classes: all match `[+-]?[0-9]+` → INTEGER (`int`); else all match `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` → REAL (`float`); else TEXT (verbatim). No non-empty fields → TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. `re.fullmatch` is required (`re.match(...$)` would accept a trailing `\n`) (Codebase Analyst §3.35).
111	- `tables()` lists stems sorted by `(s.lower(), s)` without reading contents; ambiguous stems are both listed (D14). `schema(table)` loads the table (with IO errors as above) and returns `[(column, type)]` in header order; unknown table → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 (D15).
112	
113	### 5.5 Name resolution and output names (R6, R10)
114	- Range name of a tableref = alias if present, else table name; a table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier (`emp.id` with `FROM emp e` → `unknown column 'emp.id'`). Duplicate range names (case-insensitive) → `duplicate table name 'N'` at the second tableref's range-name token.
115	- Unqualified `c` searches all FROM tables; `q.c` searches range `q`; zero matches → `unknown column 'R'`, more than one → `ambiguous column 'R'`, at the column-ref start. ON sees only tables introduced before or in its own join. Joins associate left. All name matching is case-insensitive.
116	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in FROM order; `t.*` to that table's columns; unknown/hidden `t` → `unknown table 't'` at the `t` token (D10). `SELECT *` without FROM expands to zero columns (D11).
117	- Output name: alias as written (quotes removed, `""` → `"`); else for an unparenthesized column reference (qualified or not), the column's header name from the CSV; else verbatim source text `sql[item.start:item.end]` (keeps inner whitespace/comments/newlines; e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
118	
119	### 5.6 Static typing (R7)
120	- Types: INTEGER, REAL, TEXT, NULL (bare `NULL` literal only, plus results derived per rules below). LEFT JOIN does not change a column's static type (D2).
121	- Arithmetic `+ - * / %`: operands INTEGER/REAL/NULL else `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2` at the operator. Result REAL if either REAL; else NULL if both NULL; else INTEGER. Unary `-`/`+`: operand numeric/NULL else `cannot apply 'OP' to T`; result keeps operand type.
122	- Comparisons and each `IN` item vs `x`: both numeric, both TEXT, or either NULL; else two-type mismatch (OP as written; `IN` for IN). Result INTEGER.
123	- `LIKE`: both operands TEXT or NULL, else `cannot apply 'LIKE' to T1 and T2` at the `LIKE` token; `ESCAPE` string must be exactly one code point else `ESCAPE must be a single character` at the ESCAPE string. Result INTEGER.
124	- `IS [NOT] NULL`: any operand; INTEGER.
125	- `AND`/`OR`: operands numeric/NULL else two-type mismatch (`AND`/`OR`); `NOT`: single-type mismatch (`NOT`). Results INTEGER.
126	- `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` condition of type TEXT → `condition must be numeric, got TEXT` at the condition expression's start (first character, e.g. `(` for `WHERE (name)`). Checks run bottom-up, so inner operator mismatches are reported first.
127	- Aggregates: `COUNT(*)`/`COUNT(e)` → INTEGER (any type). `SUM`: INTEGER→INTEGER, REAL→REAL, NULL→NULL (D4), TEXT → `cannot apply 'SUM' to TEXT` at the function name. `AVG`: numeric/NULL → REAL, TEXT → `cannot apply 'AVG' to TEXT`. `MIN`/`MAX`: any type, keeps argument type. Non-COUNT `X(*)` → `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT` at the `*`. Unknown name → `unknown function 'F'` at the name (checked before the `*` rule, D16).
128	- Result `types` list uses `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"`, `"NULL"`.
129	
130	### 5.7 Aggregation (R12)
131	- Aggregate query iff `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or ORDER BY.
132	- Structural identity via canonical keys after resolution: `Paren` transparent; column → `('col', table_idx, col_idx)`; literal → `('lit', TYPE, value)` (type tag so `1` ≠ `1.0`); operators by canonical op (`<>` ≡ `!=`, D8) and child keys; aggregates by upper-case name and `'*'`/argument key (Domain Expert F2).
133	- Validation (select, HAVING, ORDER BY): a node whose key matches a GROUP BY key is OK; an aggregate is OK (argument must contain no aggregate); a literal is OK; a bare column ref otherwise → `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate` at the column ref; else recurse. `*`/`t.*` → `'*' not allowed in aggregate query` at the `*`. Aggregates in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY or inside another aggregate → `aggregate function not allowed here` at that function name.
134	- GROUP BY has no ordinals or alias references (`GROUP BY 1` groups by the constant; HAVING cannot see aliases).
135	- Without GROUP BY: one group over the whole filtered input, even when empty; without HAVING exactly one row; HAVING filters to 0 or 1 row. With GROUP BY: empty input → zero rows; groups in first-seen order (dict keyed by tuple of key values; NULL equals NULL).
136	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows (including LEFT JOIN NULL-filled rows); `COUNT(e)` non-NULL values; all others ignore NULLs; over zero non-NULL values COUNT is 0, others NULL. SUM accumulates left-to-right with `+` (never `sum()`/`math.fsum`, whose float results differ across versions — Integration F23). AVG = sum/count with true division (exact int sum for INTEGER). MIN/MAX replace only on strict `<`/`>` (first seen kept on ties).
137	
138	### 5.8 Execution and evaluation order (R8, R9, R11, R13–R16)
139	Staged full passes, exactly per contract:
140	1. FROM/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; every matching pair emitted; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled right side after all pairs for an unmatched left row. No FROM → exactly one empty row.
141	2. WHERE per row. 3. Group keys then aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. HAVING per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. ORDER BY keys. 7. DISTINCT (first occurrence kept; NULL equals NULL). 8. Stable sort. 9. OFFSET, then LIMIT.
142	- Consequences: `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp LIMIT 0` raises; `SELECT 1/0 FROM emp WHERE 0` does not; select errors are reported before ORDER BY key errors; no constant folding.
143	- Evaluator compiled to closures over flat joined-row tuples; column identity `(table_idx, col_idx)` maps to a flat index.
144	- `AND`: evaluate left; if false → 0 without right; else evaluate right; false → 0; else NULL if either NULL; else 1. `OR` mirror. NULL left still evaluates right. Truthiness: nonzero true, zero false (`0.0`, `-0.0` false), NULL unknown.
145	- Arithmetic: evaluate both operands left-to-right; NULL → NULL; zero divisor (INTEGER 0 or REAL ±0.0) for `/` or `%` → `division by zero` at the operator. INTEGER `/`: `q = abs(a)//abs(b)`, negated if signs differ; INTEGER `%`: `a - b*q` (sign of dividend). REAL (either operand REAL): `/` true division, `%` `math.fmod`, operands converted with `float()`. Never `int(a/b)` or Python `%` (Integration F21).
146	- Comparisons return `int` 1/0 (never `bool`), NULL if either operand NULL. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering; numerics compare numerically.
147	- `IN`: evaluate `x` then all items left-to-right (no short-circuit, D6); NULL if `x` NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item NULL; else 0; `NOT IN` negates with 3VL. `IS [NOT] NULL` → 1/0.
148	- `LIKE`: if any operand (value, pattern, escape) is NULL → NULL (checked first, D7). Otherwise compile the whole pattern: escape char `c` followed by `%`, `_`, or `c` → literal; followed by anything else or at end → `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. Match whole-string, case-sensitive, code-point-wise with a regex-free two-pointer wildcard matcher (`%` any sequence incl. empty, `_` exactly one code point incl. newline). `NOT LIKE` negates with 3VL. Never pre-validate at analysis time.
149	- ORDER BY resolution: bare INTEGER literal → 1-based ordinal after `*` expansion (`0` or > column count → `ORDER BY position N is out of range` at the ordinal, N = `str(int value)`); bare unqualified identifier equal (case-insensitive) to exactly one explicit select alias → that output column (two → `ambiguous column 'R'`); otherwise an expression over input rows (or groups). `-1`, `(1)` are expressions. With DISTINCT each item must be an ordinal, alias, or structurally identical to a select expression, else `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used` at the expression start; such items map to output-column values.
150	- Sort: successive stable `list.sort` passes from last key to first, key `(v is not None, v)`, `reverse=True` for DESC — NULL smallest (first ASC, last DESC); ties keep pre-sort order in both directions (Domain Expert F3).
151	- `LIMIT 0` → no rows; OFFSET past end → no rows.
152	
153	### 5.9 Library API (R17)
154	```python
155	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
156	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
157	Connection.tables() -> list[str]
158	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
159	@dataclass(frozen=True)
160	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
161	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
162	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
163	```

Importing `minisql` must not alter `sys.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None` (never `bool`).
165	
166	### 5.10 Output formats (R18)
167	- Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
168	- CSV: header line, then one line per row; fields joined by `,`; every line ends `\n`. NULL → empty unquoted field. Quote a field (wrap in `"`, double inner `"`) iff it is the empty string, contains `,` `"` `\n` `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names use the same quoting. Hand-written (not `csv.writer`).
169	- Table: cell text = value text with `\n`→`\\n` and `\r`→`\\r` (two-character escapes), NULL → `NULL`; headers escaped the same way (D17). Width = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and NULL left-aligned (column alignment by the column's result type; NULL cells always left). Cells joined by ` | `; separator `-`×width joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; footer `(1 row)` or `(N rows)` (incl. `(0 rows)`); every line ends `\n`. A column of type NULL holds only NULL cells (left-aligned).
170	
171	### 5.11 CLI and REPL (R19, R20)
172	- `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`; argparse with `allow_abbrev=False`, `--data` default `.`, `--format` `choices=['csv','table']` default `None` (one-shot → csv, REPL → table), positional `sql` `nargs='?'`; `args.sql is not None` → one-shot (so `""` is one-shot with empty SQL). Usage errors: argparse exit 2.
173	- Stream setup in `cli.main()` only (never at import): `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='backslashreplace', newline='\n')`; `sys.stdin` `reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', newline='\n')` (Integration F11–F15; D18).
174	- One-shot: `connect` first (missing DIR → `IOError: …` exit 3 before lexing); execute; format the full output string, then write once. Errors: stdout empty, stderr exactly `str(err) + "\n"`; exit 1 for Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime, 3 for IO, 0 on success.
175	- Top-level guard: catch `MiniSQLError`; catch `BrokenPipeError` (redirect stdout to devnull, exit 1); `KeyboardInterrupt` (exit 130); any other unexpected `Exception` (e.g. `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`) → a single line `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <exception text>` on stderr, exit 1 (D19) — never a traceback.
176	- REPL: prompt `minisql> ` when buffer empty, `   ...> ` (three spaces) otherwise, written to stdout without newline and flushed, regardless of TTY. Input not echoed. Read lines with `readline()`; strip one trailing `\n` only (keep `\r`; D18). With an empty buffer: a line whose stripped text (strip `' \t\r\n'`) starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise append the line (joined with `\n`); when the buffer right-stripped ends with `;`, execute it and clear the buffer.
177	- Commands (exact lower-case): `.help` (free text to stdout), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line; errors as one stderr line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit`, `.exit` (exit 0). Anything else (incl. `.format` with a bad/missing argument, `.schema` with no name) → stderr `unknown command: <stripped line>` (D20).
178	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer. stdout is flushed before each stderr write.
179	- At EOF: a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. A missing `--data` DIR in REPL mode → `IOError: …` on stderr, exit 3 before the first prompt (D21).
180	
181	### 5.12 Decision register
182	
183	Decisions taken where `contract.md` is silent or researchers diverged. Each picks the option closest to the contract text; the alternative is recorded.
184	
185	| ID | Decision | Alternative (rejected) | Basis |
186	|---|---|---|---|
187	| D1 | Code targets Python ≥ 3.11 but must also run on 3.9 (no `match`, no runtime PEP 604 unions, no 3.10+ stdlib APIs, `from __future__ import annotations`). Local validation uses `python` 3.9.6. | Validate with 3.14 — the Domain Expert reported `/usr/local/bin/python3.14` available, but it is SIGKILLed on launch (exit 137, verified by orchestrator and Integration Researcher); not usable. | Environment evidence; contract requires ≥3.11 at runtime only |
188	| D2 | LEFT JOIN NULL-filled columns keep their inferred static type | Give them NULL type | "Any value may be None" |
189	| D3 | `types` entry `"NULL"` only for NULL-typed expressions (bare NULL, `-NULL`, `NULL+NULL`, `SUM/MIN/MAX(NULL)`); predicates over NULL are INTEGER | — | Contract type rules |
190	| D4 | `SUM(NULL)` → NULL type; `AVG(NULL)` → REAL; `MIN/MAX(NULL)` → NULL | Reject NULL-typed aggregate arguments | NULL type accepted wherever numeric is |
191	| D5 | CSV read by streaming `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` over the open file; first raised error wins | Decode whole file first so invalid UTF-8 always wins (Codebase Analyst A24) | Literal contract wording; oracle uses single-error files |
192	| D6 | `IN` does not short-circuit; `x` and all items evaluated left-to-right | Stop at first match | Only AND/OR are specified to short-circuit |
193	| D7 | LIKE: NULL operand checked before pattern validation → NULL | Validate pattern first | Mirrors "NULL … (checked first)" for arithmetic; "Any NULL operand gives NULL" |
194	| D8 | `<>` and `!=` structurally identical; literals identical by (type, value) | Textual identity | "same resolved columns, operators and literals" |
195	| D9 | `NOT LIKE`/`NOT IN` type errors use OP `LIKE`/`IN` at the `LIKE`/`IN` token | Position at `NOT` | Runtime LIKE errors are "at the `LIKE` token" |
196	| D10 | `q.*` with unknown/hidden `q` → `unknown table 'q'` at `q` | unknown column | Template list; table/name token |
197	| D11 | `SELECT *` without FROM → zero output columns, one row | SemanticError | Do not invent errors |
198	| D12 | Stem = `name[:-4]`; a file literally named `.csv` has stem `''` | `pathlib.Path.stem` | Contract "file stem" of `*.csv` |
199	| D13 | Non-decode OSError while reading → `DataIOError` `<file>: <strerror>` | Traceback | No-traceback rule; no template exists |
200	| D14 | `tables()` lists ambiguous stems (both) | Raise | "lists stems without reading file contents" |
201	| D15 | `schema(unknown)` → `SemanticError` `unknown table 'N'` at line 1, column 1 | DataIOError | Template exists only as Semantic |
202	| D16 | Unknown function reported before `'*'` argument rule | Reverse | Single-error oracle; name resolution precedes argument checks |
203	| D17 | Table format escapes `\n`/`\r` in header cells too | Escape only values | Preserves one-line rows |
204	| D18 | REPL stdin reconfigured to UTF-8 with `newline='\n'` (no CRLF translation; `\r` kept, lexer treats it as whitespace); stdin `errors='replace'` | Universal newlines (platform-dependent) | Byte-for-byte determinism across OSes |
205	| D19 | Unexpected internal exceptions (OverflowError, RecursionError) → one `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` line, exit 1; recursion limit raised modestly (e.g. 10000) in the parser/analyzer/evaluator entry | Traceback | "Never a traceback" |
206	| D20 | Malformed dot-commands → `unknown command: <stripped line>` | Separate usage messages | Only template given |
207	| D21 | REPL with missing DIR → IOError line, exit 3 | Start REPL anyway | `connect` raises immediately |
208	| D22 | `ambiguous table file 'N'`: N as written in the query (for `schema()`, the argument as given) | File stem | Contract N rule |

## Execution, Data Loading & Runtime Review

I reviewed HEAD 4e4f4a5 against contract.md. The files covered were `catalog.py`, `evaluate.py`, `executor.py`, `api.py`, `result.py` and `__init__.py`, with `plan.py` and `analyzer.py`/`sqlparser.py` checked where they feed the executor. For contract-silent points I used the spec's §5.4 and §5.7–§5.9 and decisions D5–D7 and D12–D19. I read the code and traced it by hand. I did not run anything; the 670-passed/2-skipped test result is the earlier evidence.

### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)
- None found.

What I traced against each criterion, all of which match the contract:

1. **Data directory and CSV** (`/Users/gkhoo-c/.Projects/mxc-c0/work/eval-c3-minisql-20261104T083537Z/minisql/catalog.py`)
   - A missing or non-directory DIR raises immediately in `connect()`, with DIR in the message as given (L27-30).
   - A fresh `scandir` runs on every call. The name test (`.lower().endswith(".csv")`) is checked before `is_file()`, so other entries are never looked at (L35-40). The stem is `name[:-4]` and lookup is case-insensitive.
   - Ambiguous stems give `ambiguous table file '<name>'` with the name as written in the query (L49-54). `tables()` sorts by `(lower(), name)` without reading files (L47).
   - Files are opened with `utf-8-sig`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(strict=True)` (L86-87). Lines with zero fields are skipped (L89).
   - Header checks: an empty name fails first, and duplicates are caught case-insensitively and report the second occurrence as written (L93-98).
   - A field-count mismatch reports `reader.line_num` after the record (L100-104). `csv.Error` reports `line_num` at the moment it is raised (L107-108). Invalid UTF-8 gives `invalid UTF-8` (L109), and an empty, BOM-only or blank-only file gives `empty file` (L113).
   - `DataIOError` is not a subclass of `OSError`, so the `except OSError` at L111 cannot wrap our own errors a second time.
   - The Python 3.11–3.13 csv docs have no change notes affecting `reader`, `strict` or `line_num` for the default dialect.
   - Tables are loaded in FROM order during analysis, before any name resolution (analyzer.py L88-99).

2. **Type inference** (catalog.py L12-13, L61-72)
   - Both patterns use `fullmatch` with ASCII `[0-9]` and no trimming, and are tried in INTEGER, then REAL, then TEXT order.
   - A column with only empty fields is TEXT, and empty fields become `None`.
   - `schema()` returns `(column, type)` tuples in header order (api.py L41-45).

3. **Numeric rules** (evaluate.py L23-46)
   - NULL is checked before the zero divisor, and the zero test (`b == 0`) catches `0`, `0.0` and `-0.0`.
   - Integer `/` and `%` use `abs()//abs()` with the sign fixed afterwards and `a - b*q`, giving -3, -1 and 1 for the contract examples. REAL uses `float()` conversion and `math.fmod`.
   - The error is raised at the operator offset (`BArith.pos`, executor.py L36-42).
   - Comparisons return int 1, 0 or `None` (L68-71). No `bool` reaches row values; `truthy()` is internal only.

4. **Three-valued logic, IN, LIKE, IS [NOT] NULL**
   - AND skips its right side only when the left is false, and OR only when the left is true. A NULL left side still evaluates the right (executor.py L53-66).
   - IN evaluates `x` and then every item, and follows the NULL rules (evaluate.py L99-108; D6). NOT IN and NOT LIKE use `not3`.
   - LIKE checks for NULL first and then compiles the whole pattern. An escape character followed by anything other than `%`, `_` or itself, or at the end of the pattern, raises `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token, which the parser records as `kw.start` (sqlparser.py L205-215).
   - Matching is whole-string and case-sensitive. I hand-traced the backtracking matcher (`%`-prefix, trailing `%`, `_`-suffix and empty-string cases) and it is correct.

5. **Execution order** (executor.py L131-211)
   - Joins are a full nested loop, and ON is evaluated for every pair with no early exit. LEFT JOIN adds one NULL-filled row after an unmatched left row.
   - Without FROM the query runs over `[()]`.
   - After that: WHERE, then group keys before aggregate arguments for each row, then HAVING, select (all rows), ORDER BY keys (all rows), DISTINCT (first projected tuple kept), and sort.
   - The sort runs one `list.sort` pass per key, last key first, with key `(v is not None, v)`. NULL never gets compared with `<`, and `reverse=True` keeps ties stable.
   - OFFSET is applied before LIMIT. Exceptions propagate before any `Result` is built.

6. **Aggregates and API**
   - `COUNT(*)` collects a 1 per row, and COUNT counts non-NULL values. SUM adds left to right and keeps INTEGER or REAL. AVG uses true division, so it is always a float. MIN/MAX replace only on a strict `<`/`>`, so the first value wins ties (L106-124).
   - Without GROUP BY there is a seeded `()` group, so empty input still gives one row, or 0/1 row with HAVING. With GROUP BY, empty input gives no rows. Groups appear in first-seen order and NULL keys group together.
   - `Result` is `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with `columns`, `types` and `rows`. Every name the contract lists is exported from `__init__.py`.

### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)
- **Integer strings over 4300 digits behave differently on Python 3.11+.** From 3.11, `int()` refuses to convert a string longer than 4300 digits and raises `ValueError`. Python 3.9.6, where the tests ran, has no such limit.
  - In `execute()`, a CSV field like that (catalog.py L72) is wrapped by api.py L33-34 into `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: Exceeds the limit ...`.
  - `Connection.schema()` (api.py L41-45) does not wrap it, so a plain `ValueError` escapes. `.schema` in the REPL may then print a traceback unless the REPL catches it.
  - The contract has no template for this, so it is very unlikely to be tested. Still, it is the one place where 3.9 and 3.11+ behave differently, and the 3.9 test run cannot show it.
- **Some numeric edge cases fall through to the generic wrapper.**
  - Examples: `float()` overflow on very large ints in REAL arithmetic, and `math.fmod(inf, x)` raising "math domain error".
  - Both end up as `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: <text>` through the D19 catch-all, not at the operator position.
  - The contract is silent on these, so they don't need fixing. It's worth knowing they exist.

### Suggestions (nice to have)
- Wrap non-`MiniSQLError` exceptions in `Connection.schema()` the same way `execute()` does, for consistency with D19.
- Coverage is adequate for every criterion above. One possible extra test: a DESC sort with ties combined with a NULL key in a multi-key ORDER BY, which would pin the "NULL last in DESC, ties stable" combination in a single assertion.

### Verdict: PASS WITH WARNINGS

I checked them against `contract.md`. Only read tools were available in this session, so I traced everything by hand and ran nothing. I relied on the existing 670-passed / 2-skipped result from Python 3.9.6 on macOS.

**Product code checks out against the contract:**
- **One-shot CLI:** exit codes 0/1/2/3 are right. `connect()` runs before lexing, so a bad data dir exits 3 first. On error, stdout stays empty because output is written only after formatting succeeds. Every unexpected exception becomes a single error line, so no tracebacks. Streams are set to UTF-8 with `\n` only inside `main()`, not at import.
- **REPL:** the prompt bytes and flushing match. So do buffering on a right-stripped trailing `;`, the commands, `unknown command: <text>`, error positions relative to the buffer, and EOF behaviour.
- **CSV and table formats:** value text, quoting (including headers and NULL), escapes, widths by code point, alignment, trailing-space stripping, the singular/plural footer, and `\n` on every line all match.
- **Error formatting and exports:** the error line format and all exported names and attributes match.
- **Stdlib-only:** every import in `minisql/` is stdlib, with no `sqlite3`.

### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)

- **[Important, confidence 90] Follow-up (a) is confirmed: the AC1 runtime import check fails falsely in common Python ≥3.11 environments.** File: `tests/test_acceptance.py:18-27`.
  - **What it does:** the child process runs `import sys, minisql`, executes a query, then flags every module in `sys.modules` whose `__file__` contains `'site-packages'` (line 23). It expects `out.stdout == b"[]\n"` (line 27).
  - **Why that fails:** `sys.modules` also holds modules that the `site` module imports at startup from `.pth` files, before any minisql code runs.
    - **Python 3.11 venv:** `python3.11 -m venv` still installs setuptools 65.5 by default. Its `distutils-precedence.pth` runs `__import__('_distutils_hack')`, which lives in site-packages. The child prints `['_distutils_hack']\n`, but the test expects `[]\n`, so AC1 fails.
    - **virtualenv, tox, nox and uv venvs:** they add `_virtualenv.pth`, which imports `_virtualenv`. The same failure happens on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.
    - **Coverage runs:** coverage's subprocess `.pth` hook has the same effect.
    - **Windows:** venv paths (`Lib\site-packages`) match the same substring.
  - **Why it matters:** this is a false failure in the target environment, not a real violation. The contract clause is AC1's "no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`", and the static AST check at lines 14-17 already enforces it correctly.
  - **Smallest fix (either one):**
    - Run the child with site processing disabled: `[sys.executable, "-S", "-c", code]`. `minisql` still imports from the cwd, and any non-stdlib import would then fail loudly with an ImportError.
    - Or diff `sys.modules` around the import: put `before = set(sys.modules)` ahead of `import minisql`, then check only `set(sys.modules) - before`.

### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)

- **Follow-up (b) is nonblocking: `BrokenPipeError` in the REPL is caught by the generic handler** (`minisql/repl.py:36-37`). A broken stdout pipe during `execute` or `.tables` hits `except Exception`. `_error` then calls `stdout.flush()`, which most likely raises again, and `cli.main` handles it (dup2 to devnull, exit 1). If that flush succeeded instead, the user would get a spurious `RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: [Errno 32] Broken pipe` line before exit 1. The contract doesn't cover broken pipes. Fix: add `except BrokenPipeError: raise` before line 36.
- **Follow-up (c) is nonblocking: the test name `test_no_sql_starts_repl_stub` is stale** (`tests/test_cli.py:132`). The test is valid, but the REPL is no longer a stub. It also overlaps `test_repl.py::test_empty_stdin`. Rename it, for example to `test_no_sql_starts_repl`.
- **CRLF input to the REPL leaves `\r` in the buffer.** `cli.py:20` reconfigures stdin with `newline="\n"`, so `"SELECT 1 +\r\n"` followed by EOF executes `"SELECT 1 +\r"`. Smallest fix: in `repl.py` after line 81, strip one trailing `"\r"` when the line ended in `"\r\n"`, which keeps the "lone `\r` is one column" behaviour.
- **`from conftest import REPO_ROOT` depends on load order** (`tests/test_acceptance.py:8`, `tests/test_contract_edges.py:17`). Both the root `conftest.py` and `tests/conftest.py` are module `conftest`, and the import only works because pytest loads `tests/conftest.py` last in the default prepend mode. It works today, but would break under `--import-mode=importlib`. Prefer `from test_imports import REPO_ROOT` or computing the path locally, as `test_imports.py:8` does.

### Suggestions (nice to have)

- `repl.py:83,93` strips only `" \t\r\n"`, while the contract says "stripped text". Python's `str.strip()` also strips `\x0b`, `\x0c` and Unicode spaces such as `\u00a0`. So a line like `"\x0c\n"` is treated as SQL rather than a blank line. This is consistent with the lexer's whitespace set and unlikely to be tested. Consider documenting the choice.
- `test_repl.py:62` makes `.TABLES` an unknown command. The contract doesn't say whether commands are case-sensitive, so this pins down unspecified behaviour. Keep it, but treat it as a design decision.
- `test_contract_edges.py:228` asserts the exact codec name `iso8859-1`. The equivalent check at `test_cli.py:189` accepts several spellings. Using the tolerant form in both places would be more robust.

### Verdict: NEEDS FIXES

The CLI, REPL, formatter and error code meet the contract byte-for-byte as far as I could trace. The verdict is NEEDS FIXES only because of finding (a): a Python 3.11 venv, or any virtualenv/uv/tox environment, will report AC1 as failed even though no rule is broken. Once that one-line test fix is in, this becomes PASS WITH WARNINGS, since (b), (c) and the other warnings are follow-ups that don't block.

### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)
- None found.

### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)
- None found.

### Suggestions (nice to have)
1. **Ordinal error text** (`minisql/analyzer.py:141`): the `N` in `ORDER BY position N is out of range` is the integer value, so `ORDER BY 007` with 3 columns prints `position 7`, not `position 007`. This follows spec §5.8, and the contract's "as written" rule covers names, not ordinals. A hidden test would only notice with a zero-padded ordinal; a one-line comment citing §5.8 would record the choice.
2. **Number literal followed by a non-ASCII letter** (`minisql/lexer.py:24`): the "followed by a letter" check uses ASCII letters only. So `SELECT 1é` gives `LexError at line 1, column 9: unexpected character 'é'`, not `column 8: invalid number literal`. This is consistent with the ASCII-only identifier rule and with spec §5.2.
3. **Case-insensitive matching** (`minisql/analyzer.py:93,122,145,220-222`): names are compared with `str.lower()`, not `casefold()`, so a non-ASCII header like `Straße` will not match `STRASSE`. The contract doesn't say which to use, and `lower()` is the likely reference behaviour; worth recording as a decision.

### Verified Against the Criteria
1. **Lexical rules:**
   - The whitespace set is exactly space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments run to `\n`, and a comment is recognised before `-` can become an operator.
   - The keyword list is exact, and keyword tokens keep their written text.
   - Doubled quotes are handled correctly in strings and quoted identifiers, including the edge cases `''''`, `""""` and an unterminated `'abc''`. Errors point at the opening quote.
   - Number forms work out as longest match because the first form needs a `.` and the third can't contain one. The bad-tail error is reported at the literal start: `1e`, `1..2` and `1_0` fail; `1.`, `1.e5` and `.5` are accepted. `1"a"` correctly lexes as a number then an alias, since `"` isn't in the tail set.
   - Two-character operators are matched before one-character ones; a lone `!` gives `unexpected character`.
   - Positions in `errors.py:7-11` are 1-based, count code points, and split lines on `\n` only.
2. **Grammar and precedence:**
   - Comparison is non-associative: `cmp` parses one tail, so a second operator fails at that operator (`a = b = c`, `a IS NULL IS NULL`, `a LIKE b LIKE c`).
   - `1 = NOT 2` fails at `NOT`, `a NOT x` fails at `x` (the longest-valid-prefix answer), and NOT/AND/OR/unary nest correctly.
   - The `name . *` item uses three-token lookahead. Aliases work with or without `AS`. Join forms are correct.
   - LIMIT and OFFSET accept only INTEGER tokens. One optional `;` is allowed, then EOF.
   - `unexpected token` uses the token's source text (strings keep their quotes, keywords keep their case). EOF is reported at `len(sql)`.
3. **Name resolution and output names:**
   - Range names come from `TableRef.range_name`, so an alias hides the table name.
   - Each `ON` sees only `scope[:i+2]`, i.e. tables up to its own join.
   - A duplicate range name is reported at the second tableref's `range_pos`.
   - Unknown or ambiguous columns are reported at the column-ref start, with `R` shown as `q.c` when qualified.
   - `*` and `t.*` expand in FROM order; an unknown qualifier gives `unknown table` (D10).
   - Output names are the alias with quotes removed, else the CSV header for an unparenthesized column ref, else `sql[start:end]`. I checked the node spans for IS NULL, LIKE…ESCAPE, IN, Call and Paren.
4. **Static typing:** the type checks are done bottom-up and match the contract tables. This covers result types including NULL, `<>` and `!=` written as typed, `IN`/`LIKE`/`AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/`SUM`/`AVG` in upper case, and `NOT LIKE`/`NOT IN` reported at the `LIKE`/`IN` token (D9). Conditions are reported at the expression start. Unknown function is checked first, then the `*` argument rule, then where aggregates are allowed. ESCAPE must be exactly one character.
5. **Aggregates:**
   - A query counts as an aggregate query if it has GROUP BY, HAVING, or an aggregate in the select list or an ORDER BY expression.
   - Structural identity uses `_key`: parentheses are ignored, columns compare by resolved index, literals by (type, value), and `<>` equals `!=`.
   - `group_level` rejects a bare ungrouped column at its ref, and `*` at the star token.
   - Aggregates are rejected in WHERE, ON, GROUP BY and inside other aggregates (`agg_ok=False`), with the error at the function name.
6. **ORDER BY and phase order:**
   - Only a bare INTEGER literal is an ordinal, counted after `*` expansion.
   - An alias must match exactly one select alias, case-insensitively; two matches give `ambiguous column`.
   - With DISTINCT, an ORDER BY expression is compared against the select keys taken before the aggregate rewrite, then mapped to that output column. The executor (`minisql/executor.py:184-203`) reads those output-index specs correctly.
   - `parse()` tokenizes all of the input before parsing. Tables are loaded in FROM order before any other semantic check.

### Verdict: PASS

"""Acceptance criteria AC1-AC11 from contract.md, with the contract's exact bytes/values."""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys

import minisql
from conftest import REPO_ROOT
from test_imports import STDLIB_ALLOWLIST, _imported_top_levels, _module_files


def test_ac1_select_one_and_import_guard(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), "SELECT 1 AS one"]) == (0, b"one\n1\n", b"")
    for path in _module_files():
        names = _imported_top_levels(path)
        assert "sqlite3" not in names, path
        assert names <= STDLIB_ALLOWLIST | {"minisql"}, path
    # Runtime: importing and running a query loads no sqlite3 and nothing from site-packages.
    code = (
        "import sys, minisql\n"
        "minisql.connect('.').execute('SELECT 1')\n"
        "bad = [m for m, mod in list(sys.modules.items())"
        " if 'sqlite' in m or 'site-packages' in (getattr(mod, '__file__', '') or '')]\n"
        "print(bad)\n"
    )
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True)
    assert out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout == b"[]\n", out.stderr


def test_ac2_select_star_and_missing_dir(run_cli, data_dir, tmp_path):
    rc, out, err = run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), "SELECT * FROM EMP"])
    assert (rc, err) == (0, b"")
    assert out == (
        b"id,name,dept,salary\n1,Ann,eng,100\n2,Bob,eng,\n3,Cid,ops,80\n4,Dee,,80\n5,Eve,ops,120\n"
    )
    assert len(minisql.connect(str(data_dir)).execute("SELECT * FROM EMP").rows) == 5
    empty = tmp_path / "cwd"
    empty.mkdir()
    assert run_cli(["--data", "missing", "SELECT 1"], cwd=empty) == (
        3,
        b"",
        b"IOError: data directory not found: missing\n",
    )


def test_ac3_schema(data_dir):
    assert minisql.connect(str(data_dir)).schema("emp") == [
        ("id", "INTEGER"),
        ("name", "TEXT"),
        ("dept", "TEXT"),
        ("salary", "INTEGER"),
    ]


def test_ac4_lex_error(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), "SELECT 1 # 2"]) == (
        1,
        b"",
        b"LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'\n",
    )
"""Library API: connect(data_dir) -> Connection with execute / tables / schema."""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from typing import List, Tuple

from .analyzer import analyze
from .catalog import Catalog
from .errors import MiniSQLError, QueryRuntimeError, SemanticError
from .executor import execute
from .result import Result
from .sqlparser import parse

_RECURSION_LIMIT = 10000


def connect(data_dir) -> "Connection":
    """`data_dir` is a str or os.PathLike; a missing or non-directory path raises DataIOError now."""
    return Connection(data_dir)


class Connection:
    def __init__(self, data_dir):
        self._catalog = Catalog(data_dir)

    def execute(self, sql: str) -> Result:
        old = sys.getrecursionlimit()
        sys.setrecursionlimit(max(old, _RECURSION_LIMIT))
        try:
            return execute(analyze(parse(sql), sql, self._catalog), sql)
        except MiniSQLError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:  # D19: RecursionError, OverflowError, int/str limits, ...
            raise QueryRuntimeError(str(exc) or type(exc).__name__, 1, 1) from None
        finally:
            sys.setrecursionlimit(old)

    def tables(self) -> List[str]:
        return self._catalog.table_names()

    def schema(self, table: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        t = self._catalog.load(table)
        if t is None:
            raise SemanticError("unknown table '%s'" % table, 1, 1)
        return list(zip(t.columns, t.types))
"""Interactive REPL: prompts, statement buffering, dot-commands; exit 0 at EOF or .quit (R20)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

from .errors import MiniSQLError
from .formatting import format_csv, format_table

PROMPT = "minisql> "
CONTINUATION = "   ...> "
_WS = " \t\r\n"

HELP = (
    "Enter SQL statements terminated by ';'.\n"
    "Commands:\n"
    "  .help                 show this help\n"
    "  .tables               list tables\n"
    "  .schema NAME          show columns of table NAME\n"
    "  .format csv|table     set output format\n"
    "  .quit, .exit          leave the REPL\n"
)


def _error(stdout, stderr, text: str) -> None:
    stdout.flush()
    stderr.write(text + "\n")
    stderr.flush()


def _guarded(stdout, stderr, action) -> None:
    """Run `action()`; MiniSQLError / unexpected errors become one stderr line (D19)."""
    try:
        action()
    except MiniSQLError as err:
        _error(stdout, stderr, str(err))
    except Exception as exc:
        _error(stdout, stderr, "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))


def run_repl(conn, fmt: str, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int:
    state = {"fmt": fmt}
    buffer = None  # None = empty buffer; otherwise the accumulated text

    def write(text: str) -> None:
        stdout.write(text)
        stdout.flush()

    def execute(sql: str) -> None:
        result = conn.execute(sql)
        write(format_csv(result) if state["fmt"] == "csv" else format_table(result))

    def schema(name: str) -> None:
        write("".join("%s %s\n" % col for col in conn.schema(name)))

    def command(stripped: str) -> bool:
        """Run a dot-command; return True when the REPL should exit."""
        parts = re.split(r"[ \t]+", stripped)
        word, args = parts[0], parts[1:]
        if word in (".quit", ".exit") and not args:
            return True
        if word == ".help" and not args:
            write(HELP)
        elif word == ".tables" and not args:
            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: write("".join(t + "\n" for t in conn.tables())))
        elif word == ".schema" and len(args) == 1:
            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: schema(args[0]))
        elif word == ".format" and len(args) == 1 and args[0] in ("csv", "table"):
            state["fmt"] = args[0]
        else:
            _error(stdout, stderr, "unknown command: " + stripped)
        return False

    while True:
        write(PROMPT if buffer is None else CONTINUATION)
        line = stdin.readline()
        if line == "":
            if buffer is not None:
                _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: execute(buffer))
            return 0
        if line.endswith("\n"):
            line = line[:-1]
        if buffer is None:
            stripped = line.strip(_WS)

"""T10: interactive REPL (subprocess bytes-mode transcripts plus direct run_repl calls)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import io

from minisql import connect
from minisql.formatting import format_csv, format_table
from minisql.repl import run_repl

P = b"minisql> "
C = b"   ...> "


def _table(data_dir, sql):
    return format_table(connect(str(data_dir)).execute(sql)).encode("utf-8")


def _csv(data_dir, sql):
    return format_csv(connect(str(data_dir)).execute(sql)).encode("utf-8")


def _repl(run_cli, data_dir, stdin, *extra):
    return run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), *extra], stdin=stdin)


def test_single_statement_table_default(run_cli, data_dir):
    table = _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1 AS one")
    assert table == b"one\n---\n  1\n(1 row)\n"
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 AS one;\n") == (0, P + table + P, b"")


def test_multi_line_statement(run_cli, data_dir):
    table = _table(data_dir, "SELECT\n1;")
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT\n1;\n") == (0, P + C + table + P, b"")

def test_eof_executes_pending_buffer(run_cli, data_dir):
    # A prompt precedes every read, so the read that hits EOF follows a continuation prompt.
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1") == (0, P + C + _table(data_dir, "SELECT 1"), b"")
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT\n1\n")
    assert (rc, out, err) == (0, P + C + C + _table(data_dir, "SELECT\n1"), b"")


def test_eof_pending_buffer_error(run_cli, data_dir):
    rc, out, err = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1 #")
    assert (rc, out) == (0, P + C)
    assert err == b"LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'\n"


def test_empty_stdin(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"") == (0, P, b"")


def test_missing_data_dir_no_prompt(run_cli, tmp_path):
    rc, out, err = run_cli(["--data", "missing"], stdin=b"SELECT 1;\n", cwd=tmp_path)
    assert (rc, out, err) == (3, b"", b"IOError: data directory not found: missing\n")


def test_crlf_input_byte_identical(run_cli, data_dir):
    lf = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1;\n.tables\nSELECT\n1;\n.quit\n")
    crlf = _repl(run_cli, data_dir, b"SELECT 1;\r\n.tables\r\nSELECT\r\n1;\r\n.quit\r\n")
    assert lf == crlf
    assert lf[0] == 0 and lf[2] == b""


def test_direct_run_repl_stringio(data_dir):
    stdin = io.StringIO("SELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1;\n.format csv\nSELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1;\n")
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    assert run_repl(connect(str(data_dir)), "table", stdin, out, err) == 0
    conn = connect(str(data_dir))
    r = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM emp WHERE id = 1")
    assert out.getvalue() == "minisql> " + format_table(r) + "minisql> minisql> " + format_csv(r) + "minisql> "
    assert err.getvalue() == ""


def test_direct_unexpected_exception_one_line(data_dir):
    class Boom:
        def execute(self, sql):
            raise ValueError("boom")

        def tables(self):
            raise KeyError("k")

    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    assert run_repl(Boom(), "table", io.StringIO("SELECT 1;\n.tables\n"), out, err) == 0
    assert err.getvalue() == (
        "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: boom\n"
        "RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: 'k'\n"
    )
    assert out.getvalue() == "minisql> " * 3

12

25	    stdout.flush()
26	    stderr.write(text + "\n")
27	    stderr.flush()

30	def _guarded(stdout, stderr, action) -> None:
31	    """Run `action()`; MiniSQLError / unexpected errors become one stderr line (D19)."""
32	    try:

42	def run_repl(conn, fmt: str, stdin, stdout, stderr) -> int:
43	    state = {"fmt": fmt}
44	    buffer = None  # None = empty buffer; otherwise the accumulated text
45	
46	    def write(text: str) -> None:
47	        stdout.write(text)
48	        stdout.flush()
49	
50	    def execute(sql: str) -> None:
51	        result = conn.execute(sql)
52	        write(format_csv(result) if state["fmt"] == "csv" else format_table(result))
53	
54	    def schema(name: str) -> None:
55	        write("".join("%s %s\n" % col for col in conn.schema(name)))
56	
57	    def command(stripped: str) -> bool:
58	        """Run a dot-command; return True when the REPL should exit."""
59	        parts = re.split(r"[ \t]+", stripped)
60	        word, args = parts[0], parts[1:]
61	        if word in (".quit", ".exit") and not args:
62	            return True
63	        if word == ".help" and not args:
64	            write(HELP)
65	        elif word == ".tables" and not args:
66	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: write("".join(t + "\n" for t in conn.tables())))
67	        elif word == ".schema" and len(args) == 1:
68	            _guarded(stdout, stderr, lambda: schema(args[0]))
69	        elif word == ".format" and len(args) == 1 and args[0] in ("csv", "table"):
70	            state["fmt"] = args[0]
71	        else:
72	            _error(stdout, stderr, "unknown command: " + stripped)
73	        return False
74	
75	    while True:
76	        write(PROMPT if buffer is None else CONTINUATION)
77	        line = stdin.readline()
78	        if line == "":

1	"""Command-line entry point: one-shot query or REPL; exit codes 0/1/2/3, never a traceback."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import argparse
5	import os
6	import sys
7	from typing import List, Optional
8	
9	from .api import connect
10	from .errors import MiniSQLError
11	from .formatting import format_csv, format_table
12	
13	
14	def _setup_streams() -> None:
15	    """D18: UTF-8 with '\\n' on every platform, whatever PYTHONIOENCODING says."""
16	    for stream, errors in ((sys.stdout, "backslashreplace"), (sys.stderr, "backslashreplace"),
17	                           (sys.stdin, "replace")):
18	        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
19	            try:
20	                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors=errors, newline="\n")
21	            except Exception:  # replaced/closed streams (e.g. under test harnesses)
22	                pass
23	
24	
25	def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
26	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="minisql", allow_abbrev=False)
27	    p.add_argument("--data", default=".", metavar="DIR", help="directory of CSV tables (default: .)")
28	    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["csv", "table"], default=None,
29	                   help="output format (one-shot default: csv; REPL default: table)")
30	    p.add_argument("sql", nargs="?", default=None, metavar="SQL", help="query to run; omit for the REPL")
31	    return p
32	
33	
34	def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
35	    try:
36	        conn = connect(args.data)
37	        if args.sql is None:
38	            from .repl import run_repl
39	            return run_repl(conn, args.format or "table", sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr)
40	        result = conn.execute(args.sql)
41	        text = format_table(result) if args.format == "table" else format_csv(result)
42	    except MiniSQLError as err:
43	        sys.stderr.write(str(err) + "\n")
44	        sys.stderr.flush()
45	        return 3 if err.kind == "IO" else 1
46	    sys.stdout.write(text)
47	    sys.stdout.flush()
48	    return 0
49	
50	
51	def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
52	    _setup_streams()
53	    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)  # usage errors: SystemExit(2) propagates
54	    try:
55	        return _run(args)
56	    except BrokenPipeError:
57	        try:
58	            os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())
59	        except Exception:
60	            pass
61	        return 1
62	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
63	        return 130
64	    except Exception as exc:  # D19: one RuntimeError line, never a traceback
65	        try:
66	            sys.stderr.write("RuntimeError at line 1, column 1: %s\n" % (str(exc) or type(exc).__name__))
67	            sys.stderr.flush()
68	        except Exception:
69	            pass
70	        return 1

166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.

191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import minisql
from test_imports import STDLIB_ALLOWLIST, _imported_top_levels, _module_files

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def test_ac1_select_one_and_import_guard(run_cli, data_dir):
    assert run_cli(["--data", str(data_dir), "SELECT 1 AS one"]) == (0, b"one\n1\n", b"")
    for path in _module_files():
        names = _imported_top_levels(path)
        assert "sqlite3" not in names, path
        assert names <= STDLIB_ALLOWLIST | {"minisql"}, path
    # Runtime: importing and running a query loads no sqlite3 and nothing from site-packages.
    # Only modules newly loaded by minisql count (startup .pth hooks may preload third-party ones).
    code = (
        "import sys\n"
        "before = set(sys.modules)\n"
        "import minisql\n"
        "minisql.connect('.').execute('SELECT 1')\n"

        " for d in ('site-packages', 'dist-packages')))\n"
        "print(bad, 'sqlite3' in sys.modules)\n"
    )

1	"""Stdlib-only guard: every import in minisql/*.py must be in the allowlist; never sqlite3."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import ast
5	import glob
6	import os
7	
8	REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
9	
10	# Explicit stdlib allowlist (do not use sys.stdlib_module_names; Python 3.9 lacks it).
11	# Tasks listing this file in scope may extend it with stdlib modules only.
12	STDLIB_ALLOWLIST = frozenset(
13	    """
14	    __future__ argparse codecs collections contextlib csv dataclasses decimal enum errno
15	    functools glob io itertools locale math numbers operator os pathlib re shutil signal
16	    stat string sys textwrap traceback types typing unicodedata warnings weakref
17	    """.split()
18	)
19	
20	
21	def _module_files():
22	    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "minisql", "*.py")))
23	    assert files, "no minisql/*.py files found"
24	    return files
25	
26	
27	def _imported_top_levels(path):
28	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
29	        tree = ast.parse(f.read(), filename=path)
30	    names = set()
31	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
32	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
33	            for alias in node.names:
34	                names.add(alias.name.split(".")[0])
35	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
36	            if node.level:  # relative import: within the package
37	                continue
38	            names.add(node.module.split(".")[0])
39	    return names
40	
41	
42	def test_only_stdlib_imports():
43	    bad = {}
44	    for path in _module_files():
45	        extra = _imported_top_levels(path) - STDLIB_ALLOWLIST - {"minisql"}
46	        if extra:
47	            bad[os.path.basename(path)] = sorted(extra)
48	    assert bad == {}
49	
50	
51	def test_no_sqlite3():
52	    assert "sqlite3" not in STDLIB_ALLOWLIST
53	    for path in _module_files():
54	        assert "sqlite3" not in _imported_top_levels(path), path
55	
56	
57	def test_guard_detects_forbidden_import(tmp_path):
58	    p = tmp_path / "x.py"
59	    p.write_text("import sqlite3\nfrom os import path\nfrom . import y\nimport numpy.linalg\n")
60	    assert _imported_top_levels(str(p)) == {"sqlite3", "os", "numpy"}
